The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.
The disclosure raises broader questions about the EU-Egypt relationship, as Egyptian authorities face scrutiny over shrinking press freedom following the jailing and alleged torture of six journalists, the entire newsroom of Matsadaash, a factchecking and investigative platform, and the closure last month of one of the country’s last independent news outlets and conviction of its high-profile editor, Lina Attalah.
Attalah is appealing against that conviction and will be in court this week as she seeks to overturn other charges including “publishing false news”, for which she was sentenced to a year in prison in absentia without her knowledge.
The spotlight is on €5bn in EU “soft” loans to Egypt – lending with easy repayment terms, known as macro-financial assistance, that is meant to be available only to countries that respect human rights and democracy. While the EU conditions on democracy and rights are vague, the loans impose much more specific requirements on Egypt to carry out economic reforms.
Separate data sources – from leaked EU documents and deleted from an Egyptian government website – raise questions about the European Commission’s claims that Egypt met targets linked to social welfare programmes, which enabled the EU to release €2.5bn in assistance.
In confidential documents, the commission told EU lawmakers that Egypt had “broadly fulfilled” and then “fulfilled” two separate targets to increase the numbers of poor people on social welfare programmes between 2024 and 2026. But data points to a net reduction of 85,734 households as the Egyptian government removed people from its welfare programmes rather than expanded coverage.
If Egypt had expanded the programmes in line with the EU’s apparent conditions – and not removed any households – about 245,000 households, equivalent to roughly 909,000 people, would be getting these benefits. (The Guardian used World Bank data to make this rough calculation).
According to the leaked documents, the commission wanted Egypt to “further expand cash transfer programmes”, but despite a net reduction in beneficiaries it gave the green light anyway to two separate “soft” loans totalling €2.5bn.
In response to the Guardian’s findings, one of the European parliament’s leading spokespeople on EU-Egypt relations, the Dutch MEP Tineke Strik, said she was introducing a question to the European Commission demanding clarification.
“The finding by this investigation that the commission is seemingly sugarcoating Egypt’s performance is worrying,” Strik said. “From the beginning, the commission has used macro-financial assistance primarily as a tool to lure Egypt into migration cooperation, while considering formal conditions and its reporting obligations towards parliament as an inconvenient formality.”
Under the plan, Egypt has so far received €3.5bn in soft loans in three instalments, with a final payment of €1.5bn expected before the end of 2027.
The charge of sugarcoating figures relates to two social welfare programmes: the Takaful and Karama cash transfer programmes for poor and vulnerable households.
The Takaful (Solidarity) programme gives poor families cash payments as long as recipients have regular health visits and good attendance at school. The Karama (Dignity) programme gives unconditional cash payments to people living with a disability, older people, orphans and widows.
One of the EU conditions for Egypt to gain the first €1bn loan was to increase the number of Takaful and Karama beneficiary households by 100,000 to 4.7 million.
In a leaked report to lawmakers in the EU council of ministers and the European parliament, the commission described that requirement as “broadly fulfilled”.
The data in that report, however, reveals a net fall of 62,281 households during this period, owing to what the EU officials describe as “a multi-annual recertification process”. Some beneficiaries were added to the list but a larger number were removed because they were deemed ineligible.
In order to achieve a later instalment of €1.5bn, Egypt was required to “further expand” the programmes, adding 60,000 households to the Takaful and Karama beneficiaries list. A second leaked report to EU lawmakers shows that the commission concluded the target was “fulfilled” because 442,118 families were added to the list.
On this occasion, the commission did not report on numbers removed. Figures from Egypt’s ministry of social solidarity, however, show a net reduction of 23,453 beneficiaries to the programmes in the 11 months until June 2026, the period leading up to the release of that payment. The EU announced the release of the €1.5bn payment in July 2026.
The data has since been deleted from the Egyptian ministry website but the Guardian has seen screenshots and archived webpages.
During a period from 2024 to 26 when the EU required Egypt to add 160,000 households to the rolls of the Karama and Takaful programmes, there was a net decline of 85,734 households.
Timothy Kaldas, the deputy director of the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, said the commission had generally “done a poor job of leveraging the funds of European taxpayers to support genuine stabilisation” on the other side of the Mediterranean. “The strategic interest of Europe is seeing a more economically stable Egypt with a population that is less precarious,” he said.
Sandra Gómez López, a Spanish socialist MEP who recently visited Cairo to assess human rights in Egypt, said the data presented by the Guardian raised important questions. “The commission must explain transparently why it considers these commitments to have been fulfilled and demonstrate that European funding is genuinely contributing to improving social protection for the Egyptian population,” she said.
She stressed that the EU should not withdraw support, “but neither can we allow the country’s strategic importance to lead us to lower our standards when it comes to human rights”.
For critics, the questions about the EU’s willingness to hold Egypt accountable on very precise socioeconomic targets do not bode well for the broader but less defined goals for democracy and human rights.
Strik said: “The fact that Egypt and the commission even seem to ignore the crystal-clear socioeconomic conditions doesn’t increase my expectation that they adhere to the vague precondition on democracy and the rule of law.”
Claudio Francavilla, an associate EU director at Human Rights Watch, said: “Without benchmarks, the EU has turned a human rights conditionality into a blank cheque for Egypt’s authoritarianism.”
In a statement to the Guardian, the European Commission said the policy target on Takaful and Karama referred to new beneficiary families “and not to its net increase”. The spokesperson said there was “no contradiction” between this statement and that in a confidential document that said Egypt was required to “further expand cash transfer programmes”.
Asked about the release of the remaining €1.5bn in promised loans, the commission said it “will be made once all conditions have been met”, referring to 24 economic policy conditions, keeping an IMF programme on track and “taking concrete and credible steps towards respecting effective democratic mechanisms, including a multiparty parliamentary system, and the rule of law, and guaranteeing respect for human rights”.
It added: “Compliance with the conditionality is examined thoroughly” by EU officials and diplomats based on “information provided by the Egyptian authorities and other relevant sources”.
Egypt’s mission to the EU in Brussels did not respond to a request for comment.

Change these settings if you want GTA 6 to feel like old GTA
There are few ways you can wind back the clock.
Grand Theft Auto 6 has many new features and updates that bring the series up to date, from the intertwined Wanted and Heat systems that keep cops on the hunt for the protagonists even after they respray their car, to charging infrastructure for electric vehicles. Still, some players might be missing certain aspects of previous titles in the series that developer Rockstar Games has either moved on from or no longer made the default option.
Once GTA 6 eventually comes to PC (which could be as soon as early 2027), it's all but certain that a swathe of mods will emerge to restore gameplay elements from previous titles. However, you don't need to wait until then to wind back the clock, at least to a certain extent. There are some in-game settings you can change to restore more of a classic GTA feel, but that might come at the expense of more convenient quality-of-life improvements.
How to restore the classic GTA sprint controls
One of the ways in which Rockstar brought GTA 6 into the modern age is by making a key change to the control system. For many years, GTA players may have had to give their thumb a bit of a workout when they wanted to sprint. By default, the console versions of GTA 5 require players to mash the X button on PlayStation or A on Xbox to help them high-tail it to their destination. The settings allow you to change this so you can hold down the button instead, which is an improvement.
However, many found it inconvenient to have this core movement function mapped to a face button instead of a thumbstick. Lots of other game developers have long assigned the sprint function to the left thumbstick, so you just need to click the same thing you're using to move your character to make them speed up.
Rockstar finally got with the program in GTA 6 by assigning the run button to L3 on PS5 and LS on Xbox by default. But maybe you really hate your thumb or for some reason just really liked how the sprint function worked in the previous games.
To return to the old movement control system, hit the pause button and go to the settings. On the control scheme page, you can change the setup from Default to Classic. This assigns run/sprint to X on a PS5 controller and A on Xbox, with the crouch ability moved to L3/LS instead, and jump to Square (PS5) or X (Xbox). In an ideal world, GTA 6 would have fully remappable controls so you could set up the control system however you want. But if you really want that classic GTA feel, you can at least make this change.
How to replicate GTA 5's targeting
One of the main drawbacks of GTA 6 for me after playing the game for 12 hours is that Rockstar hasn't upgraded its shooting mechanics well enough. It's tough to aim accurately — just ask the NPC whose hand I accidentally hit while we were horsing around and doing a whole William Tell thing. The inevitable PC version of the game will at least let players use their mouse for aiming. However, there are aim assist options that can help in the meantime.
For one thing, you can use a similar targeting option to the one found in GTA 5. In the gameplay tab of the GTA 6 settings, scroll down to the combat section and change the Targeting option from Partial to Lock-On. According to the description, this means the game will try to automatically lock onto the closest target when you're aiming. If you enable the Lock-On Target Switch option, you'll be able to flick between nearby targets using the right thumbstick.
This section of the settings menu also allows you to adjust the aim assist strength to your liking. There's also a Shooting Assist option (which helps with tracking targets that are close by) and a way to enable auto-aiming for drive-by shootings. That said, if you're a crackshot with a controller and confident in your accuracy, you can go in the other direction and select the free aim Targeting option.
How to go old school with GTA 6 navigation
GTA old heads who have been with the series since the very beginning (hi!) may remember that, in the earliest games, there was no built-in navigation help other than directional arrows that only showed you where to go as the crow flies. You had to navigate the road network all by yourself, relying on your memory, perhaps a printed map and maybe some notes to help you get around. Even getting to the location where you could save your progress in GTA 2 was a pain.
Since then, we've all grown used to minimaps and compasses that help us get to where we want to go. Those are often very useful in open-world games, which have grown in vastly in scope over the last three decades.
But if you really want a challenge in GTA 6 — and a taste of what things were like in the original 1997 game — you can minimize the navigation help in the latest title. In the UI section of the settings menu, you can switch off the minimap, compass, GPS routes and in-world objective markers and largely rely on your wits.
I recommend that you don't disable all of these features, to be clear. The world of GTA 6 is vast and dense. Getting around and knowing where to go without using any of these tools would be very difficult. But, if you want a true old-school GTA feel or want to make the game as immersive as possible, tinkering with the navigation systems is something you can try. Unlink in GTA 2, though, at least you won't have to zip over to the local church to save your progress.

A ban passed in 2023 after a yearlong dispute regarding pride flags. The resolution banned all flags except for "the American flag, the flag of the State of Michigan, the Hamtramck flag, the Prisoner of War flag and the nations' flags that represent the international character of our City" from being flown on its flagpoles. In August 2026, the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the resolution. However …
… Pride flags and other flags are not banned from being flown on private property, only on city property.
In November, a rumor spread that Hamtramck, Michigan, a city with a Muslim-majority population, had banned pride flags from being flown.
Several X posts made the claim, including one (archived) by U.S. Rep. Nancy Mace, a Republican from South Carolina, who said "Democrat-run Hamtramck, Michigan, is the first U.S. city with a Muslim-majority population. And it has BANNED all pride flags. Why aren't all the rainbow people marching in the streets of Hamtramck?"
Meanwhile, Snopes readers searched the website seeking more information on the rumor.
It is true that in 2023, after a yearlong dispute about pride flags, Hamtramck's all-Muslim City Council passed a resolution banning all flags from being flown on city property, except "the American flag, the flag of the State of Michigan, the Hamtramck flag, the Prisoner of War flag and the nations' flags that represent the international character of" the city.
However, pride flags and other flags are not banned from being flown on private property. For this reason, we've rated the claim a mixture of true and false information.
The decision was controversial. Hamtramck's City Council passed it in June, which is Pride Month. This gave rise to protests and demonstrations, contrary to Mace's suggestion that people had not marched against the ban.
We reached out to the mayor and City Council of Hamtramck, asking if they intended to single out pride flags. We also contacted the Hamtramck Queer Alliance and to Mace, asking whether she realized protests had taken place in 2023. We will update this story should we receive a response.
A dispute about pride flags
According to the decision by the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, Hamtramck moved to ban all but a few specific flags after a yearlong dispute with its Human Relations Commission, which had been in charge of maintaining the city's 18 flagpoles since 2013 (Page 2):
In June 2021, the HRC's Chair, Russ Gordon, received a request to fly the Pride flag in celebration of Pride Month. Adhering to the HRC's policy, Gordon ordered a Pride flag. Because it arrived in late autumn, Gordon waited to raise the Pride flag until 2022.
In November 2021, however, Hamtramck residents elected a new City government. Amer Ghalib won the mayoral race, and several newcomers won City Council seats. After Gordon raised the Pride flag in 2022, the City's new administration asked Gordon to remove it. He refused, and the Pride flag flew through the end of the year
After the resolution banning all but a few flags from city flagpoles passed in 2023, the Human Relations Commission decided to raise the pride flag in protest:
When Gordon and another HRC member, Cathy Stackpoole, raised the Pride flag in defiance of that resolution, the City Council removed them from the HRC and stripped the HRC of its authority over the flagpoles.
This led Gordon and Stackpoole to sue the city, the City Council and Ghalib on claims of violating free-speech rights, the First Amendment's Establishment Clause and the 14th Amendment's Equal Protection Clause.
In other words, the resolution did come about after a disagreement specifically involving pride flags.
The resolution does not ban such flags to be flown on private property, however. The intent of the resolution, which was upheld in August 2026 by the 6th Circuit, was, ostensibly, not to "open the door for radical or racist groups to ask for their flags to be flown."
The federal appellate court sided with the City Council.
For further reading, Snopes has covered several rumors about Muslims in Michigan, including the claim that Muslims in Dearborn had attempted to silence church bells. We also investigated whether Hamtramck approved an ordinance allowing religious animal sacrifice.

Stacked England aim to pile on style and add to All Black misery
- Published
There is a string of symbols tattooed on to Will Stuart's left foot.
A circle, two triangles, an up arrow, another circle, R1, L2, an up arrow, a triangle, and, finally L1 three times.
If you know, in this week of all weeks, you know.
England and British and Irish Lions star Stuart is indelibly, if jokingly, stamped with a Grand Theft Auto cheat code,, external which gives your character maximum in-game sex appeal.
In the absence of the injured Stuart and his cheat code at the start of this year, England certainly lost their mojo.
They had a terrible Six Nations. They were comfortably held at bay by South Africa. Five straight defeats ramped up pressure on the squad and their staff.
Stuart has now returned from a ruptured Achilles tendon and, with him, so has England's swagger.
Against Australia and Japan, England scored 20 tries.
They are ranked top of the Nations Championship for points scored and entries into the opposition 22m. Their attack has shown dexterity of a card sharp, with the sophistication of a socialite.
Those are the sort of intricacies needed to befuddle the best defences.
"We want England to support us. We want to bring joy to them," said head coach Steve Borthwick this week.
So far, this autumn, that objective has been achieved. Twickenham has been seduced by two charismatic displays which have been high on entertainment, if low on jeopardy.
Saturday will undoubtedly be different.
New Zealand are sore. Last weekend's defeat by Wales - their first in 73 years - stung. Coach Dave Rennie's public accusation that the players had "let the country down" will have salted wounds.
He may well have said the same of the insipid performance the team put up in a 33-19 defeat by England last year, under his predecessor Scott Robertson.
The Rennie-ssance overseen by their new boss, with wins over France, Ireland and South Africa in his first few months in charge, has given way to talk of looming crisis.
All Black backs are up hard against a brick wall. And big names - Will Jordan, Jordie Barrett, Cam Roigard and Damian McKenzie - are back to blast their way out of a hole.
England have had their fun over the past couple of weeks.
One of the benefits of being in the northern half of the Nations Championship is a steadier supply of fodder.
Fiji and Japan - the two teams invited to fill out the southern half of the new competition - have won only one of 10 games between them and have a combined points difference of minus 257.
Despite last week's reverse, New Zealand - along with world champions South Africa - are where southern-hemisphere quality is concentrated. And where England's revival will be truly stress-tested.
The comeback of Stuart, and others, has been key for England.
England made a clean sweep of their last autumn campaign, with a high-calibre set of replacements key.
Any lingering final-quarter hopes for the visitors were flushed out by England's depth on the bench.
Stuart is playing the front-row super-sub once again. Fin Baxter - another long-time injury absentee - starts at loosehead, to allow England to rotate between two top-class front rows.
George Martin - an old-school second row enforcer who is recently back from his own 14-month lay-off - is on a bench, also including Henry Pollock and Marcus Smith, loaded with stardust and points to prove.
George Furbank, whose running threat and playmaking ability from deep adds an extra dimension to attack, starts at full-back after a rotten run of knocks and set-backs.
Captain Maro Itoje seems rejuvenated by a summer off. Ollie Chessum is perhaps in the best form of his life. Seb Atkinson - still only eight caps into his Test career - has brought a mix of hard running and soft skills to 12.
Will Joseph's pace, power, good form and ability to play in midfield, as well as on the wing, has thrust him right into Rugby World Cup reckoning.
England aren't at full strength. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tom Curry and Alex Mitchell are big misses. Sam Underhill and Guy Pepper too.
But injuries are inevitable. And England, at the moment, are relatively fully loaded.
"The last time we had this depth was a year ago," Borthwick said, drawing an implicit link back to England's purple patch of 12 straight wins through 2025 and the very start of 2026.
The mood music, like the performances, has been good.
Itoje suggested there was a renewed sense of purpose and ownership in camp. Borthwick credited the players with leading a successful drive to improve discipline.
Attack coach Lee Blackett's fingerprints are all over some of the attacking shapes thrown over the past fortnight.
The momentum is real.
Victory over New Zealand, of any kind, would stomp the accelerator to the floor.
If it comes with eye candy, all the better.

As Kolkata choked on toxic air following Diwali and Kali Puja celebrations, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari accused those raising concerns over firecracker pollution of being communists opposed to Hindu traditions. His remarks were consistent with the concerted push by a section of the Right wing to portray criticism of firecrackers as an attack on Hindu religious practices. However, among those complaining about noise levels and pollution in Kolkata were members of Adhikari’s own party and cabinet.
The Bengal CM made the remarks while addressing the media during a visit to the coastal town of Digha on Monday, where he had gone to attend an administrative meeting and visit the Kali Puja organised by the Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Traders Association.
Speaking to reporters, Adhikari said, “There has been an awakening of Sanatan in this state, and some people have a problem with that. The people making these allegations (about firecrackers) had turned Hindu religious festivals into cultural fests… These people do not apply ‘tika’ or religious markings on their foreheads, they do not wear ‘dors’ or religious threads on their wrists, nor do they wear tulsi beads around their necks.”
Adhikari further said, “The communists are raising this issue of firecrackers. We have controlled it in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directives. Firecrackers were burst in some places even after 10 pm, and the police took necessary action. We have stopped DJs, and we do not want environmental pollution. But people will have fun during Diwali. They will celebrate with lights and burst firecrackers. Where is the problem with that?”
While acknowledging that firecrackers had been burst beyond the time limit prescribed by the Supreme Court, Adhikari sought to deflect criticism by pointing to action taken by the administration.
“Those complaining that sound crackers were burst for a few hours longer than the time stipulated by the Supreme Court should know that the Pollution Control Board and the police are taking action against such violations. I would request those complaining about firecrackers to also congratulate the state government for stopping DJs. I will not say that DJ incidents did not happen in remote corners, but I did not hear them blaring, at least near the roads,” he said.
Firecrackers can Cure Diseases, Says Bengal Minister, then Apologises
According to the Supreme Court’s directives, only green firecrackers were allowed to be burst between 8 pm and 10 pm on Diwali. However, statements by ministers, the West Bengal Police’s deletion of a post urging responsible Diwali celebrations, and the general perception that a BJP government would not impose restrictions on Hindu festivals had collectively sent out a clear message: When it came to celebrating a majoritarian festival, the rules could be bent, if not ignored altogether.
BJP leader and Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikary said on Monday, “Our honourable chief minister has said that people will definitely burst firecrackers. How can we celebrate Kali Puja without firecrackers? But we will burst them in accordance with the instructions of the local police station. Also, many diseases can be prevented simply by lighting firecrackers.”
Although Adhikary later apologised and backtracked on her statement, claiming that the media had misinterpreted her remarks, the message had already got across.
A section of social media users also began targeting dissenting voices who tried to reason with their fellow citizens. A user named Partha Pratim Kundu, who describes himself as a wildlife photographer, asked in a post how elderlies, children and birds and animals survived in earlier times when there was no curb on firecrackers.
Another Facebook user, Chayan Mukherjee, who hailed the chief minister’s indulgence on firecrackers, claimed in a post that “most of the Indian environmentalists and human rights activists, as well as professors at various institutions, receive funding from outside to oppose the country’s development.”
Domkal’s CPI(M) MLA Mostafijur Rahaman Rana had urged people to celebrate Diwali as a festival of lights, without noise and loud firecrackers. BJP MLA Tarunjyoti Tiwari gave the issue a communal twist by asking whether the legislator would also call for a ‘bloodless Eid’.
State BJP leader Keya Ghosh also criticised Mostafijur Rahaman for advocating a noise-free and smoke-free Diwali.
The lone CPIM MLA of West Bengal had wished smokeless, soundless Diwali.

The political messaging was accompanied by widespread violations on the ground. A large section of the public openly flouted firecracker regulations. Kolkata’s AQI reached 623 around 11 pm on Sunday night, reported The telegraph. At 12.51 am on Monday, IQAir classified the city’s air quality as hazardous, recording an AQI of 532, with PM2.5 at 342 and PM10 at 405. Both particulate matter concentrations were several times higher than the WHO’s recommended limits.
Left with no other option, residents in several localities took matters into their own hands, protesting against the rampant bursting of firecrackers and intervening to stop it. Facebook user Anitesh Chakraborty narrated his experience in a post.
Chakraborty went up to a neighbouring apartment’s rooftop around 1.45 am to ask people bursting firecrackers to stop. While some residents supported his objection, others on nearby rooftops mocked him with gestures and taunts. Nevertheless, the intervention succeeded in stopping the firecrackers. He observed that the rooftops of apartment buildings had become spaces where people felt free to flout restrictions, and argued people to raise their voices against such violations.
According to a report by the Times of India, by 1 am, the West Bengal Pollution Control Board had received 84 noise-related complaints, while Kolkata Police had recorded 434 complaints.
Police rounded up 371 people for bursting illegal firecrackers, arresting 205 of them. Another 387 people were arrested for disorderly conduct. Several commentators pointed out that the most effective way to curb the use of illegal firecrackers was to stop their manufacture and sale. This year, only 238.6 kg of such products were seized, compared to 853 kg last year.
Kolkata’s high-rise buildings were particular hotspots for violations of firecracker and noise restrictions. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari himself acknowledged that the rules could not be enforced in every high-rise apartment building, as the state did not have enough police personnel.
Even hospitals located in silence zones were not spared. According to a report by The Telegraph, areas near hospitals such as B C Roy, R G Kar, M R Bangur and Sishumangal also faced onslaught of loud firecrackers.
To Celebrate Responsibly or Not? Bengal Police in a Fix
Signs of this situation had emerged earlier, when the West Bengal Police deleted a firecracker awareness post within hours of publishing it, as previously reported by Alt News.
Published on the morning of November 5 with the caption, “Please celebrate responsibly. It’s our Diwali too!”, the AI-generated poster featured two stray cats and a dog shivering due to the loud noise of firecrackers. However, it was deleted within three hours.
The post’s comment section was flooded with threatening messages directed at police and familiar Right-wing arguments, including questions about whether the police would also call for a ‘bloodless Eid’ and why the police and administration interfered only in Hindu festivals.
Similarly, Delhi Police, too, deleted a firecracker awareness post, while the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) removed a video featuring actor Dia Mirza advocating for a pollution-free Diwali from its social media accounts. Both decisions followed social media outrage from BJP-RSS supporters who claimed that the posts hurt Hindu religious sentiments.
A similar message by AISA leader Neha Bora also faced backlash from the far-right social media ecosystem.

BJP MLAs Complain about Noise Levels
Although a section of the Right wing encouraged unrestrained celebrations during Diwali and Kali Puja in the name of upholding Hindu traditions, some voices within the BJP struck a different note.
BJP leader and Sonarpur Dakshin MLA Roopa Ganguly tagged Kolkata Police in a post on Facebook stating she was unable to sleep because of the noise of firecrackers. However, the post is no longer available now.
State urban development minister Agnimitra Paul was seen roaming around the city in a police vehicle, attempting to curb the firecracker menace.
Paul said, “Please think about other people. Consider the condition of the elderly and the sick. The firecrackers are bursting so loudly that my heart is trembling.”
However, these interventions came too little, too late. The ruling dispensation had, through its rhetoric and its reluctance to enforce restrictions, effectively given people a free hand to flout the law, with the environment and public health bearing the consequences.

Kimi Antonelli was 10 when his father Marco first realised the boy sitting on his lap, operating the steering and gears, might have an exceptional talent as a racing driver.
The pair were at the Adria circuit in north-east Italy, Marco with his Lamborghini sports car team, Kimi competing in a karting race.
It was the end of the day and Marco, a former driver himself, asked his son: "Do you want to try the Lamborghini?"
Of course he did.
Marco strapped himself and Kimi into the car, belts extended around both. Dad was in charge of the throttle and brake, his son would control the rest.
"I couldn't see the track because he was in front of me with a helmet on," Marco tells BBC Sport. "I could only see beside me the marker panels before each corner - 100m, 50m.
"We started to drive, step by step, faster, faster, faster. In the end, I pushed like I was alone and I arrived at the braking point at the end of the straight, 320km/h, braked very hard and at the limit.
"The car had a lot of oversteer. Kimi controlled the oversteer perfectly, then I went on the throttle, Kimi finished the oversteer, changed gear, and went.
"I said: 'OK, stop, because it has now become dangerous.' But when I saw the video, 10 years old, on my leg, oversteer, everything perfect, I said: 'Maybe he has something special.'"
And now Kimi, who turned 20 only in August, has dominated F1 in only his second season, and become the youngest world champion in the sport's history.
This is the story of a boy his dad says was "born in a garage".
"Kimi from 15 days old was in the garage and heard the sound of the engine and the smell of the exhaust," says Marco, who worked with his wife Veronica on their racing team business.
It was the Christmas holidays when Kimi was about three, and Marco had brought home a simulator he had bought for his guests to try out at the Bologna Motor Show.
"Each evening, Kimi wanted to drive," Marco remembers.
Just like seven years later in the Lamborghini, Kimi would sit on Marco's leg, the controls divided in the same way.
"I remember one night I started to fall asleep because I had been at work very early and we had a crash because I didn't brake when we arrived at the end of the straight," Marco says.
"And Kimi said: 'Dad, dad, no sleep, no sleep. I have to drive.'"
Marco Antonelli did not originally want his son to become a racing driver, because of his own struggles during his career.
"Sometimes you are fast but not in the right position to become a professional driver," he says.
In the 1990s, Marco Antonelli was on the cusp of becoming a works driver in the DTM touring car series, then a huge hit with audiences across Europe.
He tested for Alfa Romeo, but then the team boss left and the opportunity evaporated. Another chance came up with BMW, alongside Roberto Ravaglia and Steve Soper - stars at the time. Again, the same thing happened.
"I suffered a lot for it," Marco says. "And, of course, I was scared that my son [would] relive the same situation. At the beginning, I was very stressed about the passion my son had for motorsport."
Kimi tried a go-kart for the first time when he was five, and immediately showed an awareness of racing lines, braking points and car control.
The Antonellis were what Marco describes as "a normal family". They could not possibly afford to pay for Kimi to take part in all the categories on the way to Formula 1.
Marco decided he could fund Kimi through karting and a year of the basic single-seater category, Formula 4. After that, he figured he might be able to put him in one of his GT cars and become professional that way.
But Kimi immediately started to impress. Whatever category he entered, he was quick, and won.
By the time Kimi was 11, his name was buzzing around motor racing circles. Mercedes heard about him, and their driver academy scout Gwen Lagrue flew to Italy to check him out.
It was a season in which Antonelli had ended up driving a kart with less power than those of his rivals. Marco had told Kimi this would be good for him - he should think not about the result, but about how to improve, always push hard.
"Gwen was impressed about this condition of power and driving in this category that Kimi did," Marco says. "And maybe they understood that Kimi was a different child."
Now Kimi was a member of the Mercedes driver academy, Marco could stop worrying about money, and start focusing on helping his son achieve his full potential.
Mercedes were not the only big names in F1 who had noticed Antonelli's promise.
"When he was in karting, you could already see he was one of the stand-out talents," says four-time world champion Max Verstappen, the only other teenager to win an F1 race.
At 15, Antonelli was ready to move up to cars, and, as a final preparation, did a couple of races in a karting category with gears. On his debut, with minimal pre-event testing, he took pole position. After that, he went to the world final, and stuck it on pole again.
This was the end of 2021, after which Antonelli moved full-time into cars. Through 2022, he swept the board in various championships in Formula 4, and the same happened in Formula Regional in 2023.
1 of 4
By now, Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff was already thinking that Antonelli would be his next F1 driver, potentially a replacement for Lewis Hamilton. With the seven-time champion approaching 40, Wolff was planning on taking control of that generational transition.
So when it came time to negotiate a new contract with Hamilton in 2023, Wolff played hardball. Hamilton wanted to sign for at least two firm years, Wolff only one. In the end, they compromised on a contract for 2024 with an option for 2025.
Hamilton, unimpressed, decided to look at his options, and signed to join Ferrari in 2025, telling Wolff in late January 2024, before the start of that season.
Wolff immediately phoned Marco Antonelli, to tell him the "very big news".
"'We put Kimi in Formula 1,'" Marco remembers Wolff saying. "'What do you think?'
"I said: 'Oh, [it] is a difficult question you ask me. Of course I'm happy that you think about Kimi but are you sure he's ready?'"
Mercedes were at a management away day. Wolff called his senior engineers together to tell them about Hamilton's decision.
"We were reviewing options and trying to come to a fairly rapid conclusion," says trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin.
"We were all keen to just go with Kimi, which we knew was a bit of a risk. But it was quite exciting and we thought, based on his career to date, he had a good chance of being very good. It seemed like a good challenge."
Antonelli had not even driven an F1 car when Wolff made the call. Mercedes put together a testing programme for him, 20-odd days in cars a couple of years old at tracks all over the world to prepare him for his F1 debut in 2025.
Shovlin and the engineers were immediately impressed.
"It was how rapidly he would get up to speed," Shovlin says. "What you normally see with drivers is they're just incrementally going a little bit quicker, braking a bit later.
"If you compare with other drivers we've seen in an F1 car for the first time, the best I'd ever seen until then was George [Russell]. You suddenly saw someone who was quite similar.
"With Kimi, he took a couple of runs to work out how the car behaved and then he'd be more or less on the limit.
"The other thing you can see is the fidelity of the car control, how they can sit with it right on the edge of breaking away from them on entry to a corner, but they can just control it in that condition.
"Equally, when you looked at the mistakes he was making, they were often errors of judgement or lack of experience. They weren't run-out-of-talent mistakes."
Antonelli made one of these at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix. Wolff decided to give him his first experience of an F1 weekend in first practice at his home race at Monza.
It was a spectacular debut - for both good and bad reasons.
Antonelli set the fastest time on his first lap. Then he went for another. He was flying, miles quicker than anyone up to that point, but then he crashed heavily at the final corner, Parabolica.
"No-one on earth could have got the car around the corner at the speed he was attempting," Shovlin says. "He clearly got into his head that he would try and do something special and it was an error of judgment."
Wolff took Antonelli aside, told him it was OK, and not to worry about it. But the crash had a significant impact on Antonelli.
Wolff was very clear in public about managing expectations of Antonelli going into his debut season.
"I conditioned myself so strong that I said: 'There's going to be moments of brilliance and moments where you want to tear your hair out'," Wolff says.
There were stand-out moments, including pole for the sprint in Miami.
But the middle part of the season, through Europe, was a disappointment. A change to the rear suspension design made the car nervous and rocked his confidence. His pace was not impressive, and he made too many mistakes.
"We expected more highlights from him," Shovlin says.
Marco Antonelli explains: "Mercedes needed to have a good result after a period that was not like the Hamilton era. And, of course, needed two cars that always take points.
"Kimi felt this necessity. The crash in Monza was very tough for him to forget. It created on him a big pressure."
Wolff said the "moments of brilliance were there" but then there was "a spell of nine races that was really not good".
"Me, personally, I never doubted," says Wolff. "Other people doubted. In the team and externally."
A year on from his practice debut, Antonelli crashed again in Monza practice.
"This was the point where I said: 'Kimi, you've got to turn this around. This is just not good enough'," says Wolff. "He said: 'I know.'"
Marco Antonelli says he and his son talked a lot during this period and that Kimi "understood that everything can change".
"The period was bad but you can see light at the end of the tunnel," he says. "And step by step he started to take confidence."
Once F1 had left Europe in the autumn of last year, there was a shift.
"Suddenly, we felt like we were making really good progress," says Shovlin.
"There were signs towards the end of the year. I'm not saying any of us thought we'd see what we've seen so far this year, but that we had a decent F1 driver."
Antonelli has been rather more than that this year. He took the season by storm, and established a consistent supremacy over Russell.
In the best car in the field, Antonelli took six poles and six wins in the first 11 races, establishing a 50-point lead in the championship.
Mercedes lost their dominant form in the second half of the season in the face of challenges from first McLaren and then Red Bull.
But Antonelli remained a consistent threat at the front, and he killed off his Monza ghosts in the Italian Grand Prix with a stunning victory after an engine penalty led to him starting 19th on the grid.
He put in a drive of clinical excellence and, with help from a safety car, chased down and caught Russell in the final laps to take a win that will go down in folklore.
The extent of his turnaround in form has shocked almost everyone.
"We were all surprised," Wolff says. "My thoughts were always that he needed to make the experience of knowing all the tracks, the pressure of performing on such a high level under the spotlight of the media, the constant public feedback, whether you're doing well or not, the situations everyone wanted to be close to him.
"There wasn't one single defining factor where I would have said that made it difficult for him, but this year, he knew exactly what to expect. What was really nice to see is that the self-confidence, without feeling any entitlement, has shone."
Marco points to his son's "very strong" mentality.
"In F4 and Freca, he started with not good results, and he was able to remake everything and, at the end, work hard and win the championship," he says.
"We talk about F1. I don't know what the spark is in his brain, but Kimi in the past did the same."
Verstappen says: "For me, there was never any doubt that he would make the jump the year after and already be a lot more consistently competitive.
"It's normal in the progression of a driver. In your rookie season, it can be quite tough, but at the moment, of course, he's doing an amazing job."
Kimi pays tribute to his father, describing him as his "rock", while Wolff also praises the driver's "typical Italian family".
"They are caring, they are loving," Wolff says. "Kimi's character, he's gentle, he has empathy, he has charisma, he has the right amount of intelligence for being a racing driver."
Mercedes have been talking to Antonelli about managing his emotions, which have flared at times this season, such as in the sprint in Canada, when the racing between the two Mercedes drivers came close to boiling over.
Shovlin says: "He just says: 'I'm young, I'm Italian, what do you expect?'"
The remark reveals Antonelli's sense of humour, but also a maturity and self-awareness that might not always be expected in someone so young.
Wolff says: "He has all that. He's actually not [fitting the stereotype of] a typical emotional Italian. He's so clear [in] what he needs to do in a car. I don't see lots of emotion. I see full focus, full concentration. I see, 'OK, this is a problem, let's analyse it, and move on.'
"You see him in a debrief afterwards. You couldn't really say whether there was a bad or a good session. It's all very balanced and stable."
Antonelli took advice on this when he met tennis legend Roger Federer at Wimbledon this summer.
"We chatted about my races," Antonelli says. "About when he used to play, and about life in general.
"About pressure, he just told me to focus on one race at a time, just focus on what you can control, and also to control the emotions, especially the ones that can make you do mistakes."
Federer's words echoed something Marco has always impressed on his son.
"In our family, we use this concept in normal life as well," he says.
"We have to live every day our best day. You work hard every day to arrive at the end of the project you have."
Back in February 2024, Wolff followed up his phone call to Marco with a meeting in Milan.
"Toto said 'Of course it will be difficult, but I think after one year of experience, we can do very well with Kimi in F1'," Marco says.
"The project was 2025 experience, 2026 start to achieve results. I think we overachieved."

The Mundka monitoring station of the Delhi Pollution Control Board recorded a PM2.5 concentration of 3,744 µg/m³ at 2 am on the Diwali night, which is 60 times the standard measure. Yes, you read it right. 60 times. Reports emerged the next day that 93 of the top 100 cities with worst AQI were from India following Diwali celebrations on November 8. AIIMS pulmonologist Vijay Hadda told ANI on November 9, “I am honestly surprised that we are still alive. I do not think this kind of air is suitable for human survival.”
In any country with a functional government, this would warrant the environment minister to at least make a statement, even if not take direct accountability. Not in India.
Union minister of environment, forest and climate change, Bhupender Yadav, has remained conspicuously silent on the country’s deteriorating air quality before or after Diwali.
From the days preceding Diwali to four days after the festival when this article is being written, Yadav neither issued a single public appeal urging citizens to responsibly engage in celebrations, nor used his social media handles to spread awareness about the environmental consequences of bursting firecrackers or to address the mounting pollution crisis affecting major parts of the country.
Did Bhupender Yadav go Missing from Public Platforms?
Far from it. Yadav remained active on social media throughout this period. Between November 1 and November 12, he made 29 posts on his X account. Not one of them addressed the worsening air pollution, deteriorating air quality across Indian cities, or the need for public awareness and precautionary measures.
The days before Diwali are also crucial because pollution levels skyrocketing on the day of the festival and immediately after has become an annual phenomenon. It is reasonable to expect the minister holding the environment and climate change portfolio to make a public appeal ahead of Diwali, more so because firecracker pollution has been a matter of contention and has reached the Supreme Court in recent years.
Clearly, the Alwar MP thinks otherwise.
Modi Reigns Supreme on Yadav’s X Timeline
On November 7, observed as Chhoti Diwali, and November 8, the main day of Diwali, Yadav shared nine posts. These included amplification of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Diwali greetings to citizens, Modi’s Diwali celebrations and interactions with jawans at the CoBRA (Commando Battalion for Resolute Action) Operations Base in Karanpur, in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar district, as well as Yadav’s own festive greetings.
On November 7, Yadav shared a video of Narendra Modi greeting fellow citizens with wishes for Diwali and shared that, like every year, he would celebrate Diwali with the “veer jawans” of the country.

Updates on Political Assignments etc
A review of Yadav’s remaining social media activity during this period shows that he continued to document his political engagements, meetings with public representatives, participation in political programmes and official engagements.
On November 1, Yadav attended the “Save democracy, remove anarchy” rally alongside the Maharashtra chief minister and deputy chief minister. The following day, he met the Governor of Uttarakhand. On November 3, he met Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami and Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary in Delhi.
On November 5, he shared another post about his participation in the ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ protest in Darbhanga, Bihar. He also posted about his visit to the residence of senior BJP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ravindra Kishore Sinha, where he met Sinha’s son, Rituraj Sinha, and other family members and paid his respects.
On the same day, Yadav addressed the media in Patna on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, alleging that ‘planned attacks are being carried out on the country’s constitutional institutions by the Congress’.

On November 9, he attended the funeral of Dr Jaswant Yadav, the MLA from Bahror and former Member of Parliament, alongside the Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma.
His latest post, on November 12, documented an interaction chaired by him with Indian LeadIT (Leadership Group for Industry Transition) member companies and project partners in New Delhi.
In addition to these engagements, five of Yadav’s posts during the November 1–12 period were dedicated to sharing decisions taken by the Union Cabinet on various policy matters.
Despite maintaining a steady stream of updates on his political engagements, official meetings and public appearances, the environment Mminister’s X account offered no indication of concern over the environmental consequences of the widespread bursting of firecrackers during Diwali. Neither before it. Nor after.
Incidentally, on October 30, Yadav posted about an integrated command and control centre in Delhi to review and monitor air pollution real-time across Delhi-NCR.
The Firecracker Pollution Debate was Raging Since October 25
As early as October 25, Delhi Police had shared a video on its X handle urging citizens not to burst crackers this Diwali. The post said: “This festive season, let tails wag, not tuck. Say NO to crackers, YES to a greener Diwali.” Soon after it was posted, social media users predicted that it would be taken down. Delhi Police proved them right, deleting the post within hours.
The episode sparked a debate, with a section of the Right-wing putting forward what has become its usual pre-Diwali stance on firecracker pollution: that any call to shun firecrackers or celebrate with restraint is an affront to Hindu faith. The debate intensified when Bengal Police did much the same thing, posting about “responsible celebrations” before deleting the post, and the Mumbai civic body took down a similar post featuring actor Dia Mirza.
Yadav, it appears, has been blissfully unaware of all this.
There were no cautionary appeals ahead of the festivities urging citizens to celebrate responsibly or remain mindful of the deteriorating air quality and the environmental and health hazards associated with firecrackers. Nor did Yadav acknowledge the worsening situation in the aftermath of the celebrations, when several Indian cities were engulfed in thick layers of smog, and the country dominated global rankings of the most polluted cities.
Alt News has reported that on the morning after Diwali, the front pages of all major English dailies were dominated by news about severe air and noise pollution in most cities in north and central India.

As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.
“Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.
The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.
“Agents are not programmed so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see, the exploration space that we have to address is huge and the web is hostile,” says Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgement when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”
Building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed quickly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.
Even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome users on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.
The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.
“We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” says Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step, there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”

If your Android phone’s battery drains too quickly, try enabling auto-brightness, using dark mode, limiting background apps, reducing screen timeout, and turning off unused features. These 15 practical tips can improve battery life and help maintain battery health.
I cannot function without my phone. It makes my experience better during my walks, jogs, and all other activities throughout the day. Unfortunately, I have to charge my phone multiple times a day or keep a power bank as a backup, just in case. The ease created by my Android phone is instantly undone by the quickly draining battery. Along with the phone, I should carry a cable, an adapter, and a power bank.
In that frustration, I started looking into why my Android phone battery was draining fast. I checked the battery usage data, identified what was causing the drain, and fixed those issues. Now, my battery lasts longer. These are the tips that helped me improve the battery life on my Android phone.
Table of Contents
Android Phone Battery Draining Fast? Try These 10 Tips
I used these tips to improve my Android phone’s battery life on a single charge. You can use the tips that work for you without sacrificing the functionality you need.
Enable Auto Brightness
Brightness affects how visible the display is, irrespective of the light in our surroundings. When we keep the brightness too high, it affects our eyes in the dark. In addition to that, the battery drains too quickly when powering the high brightness for your phone’s display.
If we keep the brightness low, it affects the visibility of our phone’s display during daytime when we are out in the open under the sun. To not affect the visibility and save the battery from draining quickly, we can enable Auto Brightness on our phone.
The auto-brightness feature on our phones adjusts the brightness of our display based on the light in our surroundings. For example, when you are outside where there is abundant sunlight, the auto-brightness feature increases the brightness to make visibility better for you. Similarly, it decreases the brightness when you are in a dark or dimmed environment.
To enable auto-brightness on your phone, open the Settings app and go to Display or Display & brightness settings. The jargon for options varies by manufacturer.
Find Brightness options and toggle the button beside Auto brightness to enable it. You will see the brightness of your screen increase or decrease as per your environment in real time.
Enable Dark Mode
Android phones with OLED or AMOLED displays consume more power for display. If it is set to light mode, a major chunk of battery life goes to power. Setting the screen to dark mode makes it easier on the battery. The battery does not need to power the entire display by switching off the black pixels.
You can enable dark mode in the display settings of your phone. Open the Settings app and find the display settings. Set the display mode to Dark mode.
Dark mode, at first, may look odd. Once you get accustomed to it, there is no going back.
Disable Always-On Display
Always-On Display consumes a significant amount of power from the battery. The display always shows time or notifications even when you are not using the phone actively.
You must disable the Always-On Display feature if you do not have any use for it. Open the Settings app on your Android phone and search for Always-On Display. It will show the option. Tap on it. Toggle the button beside Always-On Display to turn it off.
It may not reduce battery drain noticeably, but small things like these can help optimize battery life.
Set Screen Refresh Rate to Auto
The screen refresh rate feature on Android gives us a smoother display experience. Manufacturers flaunt the screen refresh rate while launching and advertising new smartphones. The higher the refresh rate of a screen is, the more battery it consumes. If you are not a gamer or do not use your phone for experiences that demand a higher refresh rate, you may set the Screen refresh rate to Auto.
Open the Settings app on your phone, search for refresh rate, and open the refresh rate options. Then, set the refresh rate to Auto or Auto-select. Instead of using a higher refresh rate that consumes more battery, your phone now optimizes the screen refresh rate based on the app or activity for a smoother experience. You may also set it to Standard or anything that offers a 60 Hz refresh rate to extend battery life.
If you are a gamer, Auto refresh rate would be the best option.
Decrease Screen Off Time
Screen off time is something we mostly overlook when looking to optimize battery on our phones. If the screen off time is set to a longer time, it consumes battery and aids in draining faster. Small things like these add up and drain the battery.
Open the Settings app on your phone and search for screen off. You can find the Screen off feature in Display settings. Tap on the Screen off or Auto Screen off options (based on your manufacturer) and select a shorter time.
Now, when you do not use the phone, the screen will be turned off as per the time you have selected. The shorter the time, the more you optimize the battery.
Disable Unnecessary Sounds and Vibrations
Sound and vibration for ringtones and notifications are okay. But touch vibrations, keyboard sounds, dial pad tones, lock sounds, and other such sounds or vibrations when we do something on our phone are not necessary. They stress the battery and make it drain faster.
Disabling those unnecessary sounds and vibrations enhances the battery life and saves you from charging the phone frequently.
Open the Settings app on your phone and go to Sound & vibration settings. Go to More sounds (on OxygenOS) or similar settings where you can enable or disable additional sounds, based on your manufacturer.
Then, disable the sounds that you feel are unnecessary by toggling the buttons beside them.
This can optimize battery life, and you can notice the difference within a few hours. Additionally, you can tweak the vibration intensity to optimize your battery further regarding sound and vibration settings.
Check for Apps That Use a Lot of Battery
Android provides detailed battery data where we can see which app is consuming more battery, how long each charge lasts, etc. Using the battery data, we can optimize the apps that consume a lot of battery or install alternatives that consume less battery.
We can access the battery data through the Battery settings. Open Settings and go to Battery settings on your device. Scroll down to the Battery usage by app section in the Battery settings and see which app is using more battery. Tap on the app that is consuming a lot of battery.
It opens the detailed view of battery consumption in the last 24 hours. You can also see options to control battery consumption for the particular app by restricting background activity, etc. Select Restrict background activity if you want to optimize battery and extend its life.
If you want the app to run in the background, you can set it to Smart mode if your manufacturer provides such an option. Repeat the process until you restrict all the power-hungry apps on your device. This significantly improves the life of your battery in each charge.
Turn On the Option to Enter Power Saving Mode Automatically
In the Battery settings, you will find Power saving settings or options. Go to Power saving settings and toggle the button beside Automatically enter Power saving mode. Then, set the battery percentage that should trigger the power saving mode on your device.
Your device will enter Power saving mode when it triggers the battery percentage you set, and it will last longer.
Disable WiFi, Mobile Data, Location, and Bluetooth When Not in Use
You might have noticed your phone battery drains quicker than normal when you pair Bluetooth devices or use location actively. It is better to turn them off when you do not use them.
Keeping WiFi, mobile data, location, and Bluetooth on, even without any usage, consumes a good amount of battery. When you are not actively using any of them, turning them off saves you some battery.
Turn Off Additional Features
There are many features that we rarely use, but consume a good amount of battery. They are live wallpapers, widgets that we do not use, opening web pages and leaving them running in the background, manufacturer apps that run automatically, etc.
Disabling or turning them off saves us a lot of battery. In addition to them, when we install a new app, it asks for notification permissions, location permissions, etc. Disabling notifications for unimportant apps also saves our battery from draining quickly.
These tips, when used together, will optimize your Android device’s battery and extend its life in each charge cycle. Even after doing all this, the battery may drain quickly due to deteriorated battery health. Let’s see how to check and optimize battery health on Android.
How to Optimize Battery Health on Android
The battery on our Android phone degrades with use, and the health drops from 100% to lower levels. The lower the health of your battery, the less power it stores. The capacity keeps on degrading. This is not limited to iPhones. Android phones also started showing battery health. It depends on your manufacturer.
To check the battery health on your Android, you can use third-party apps like Battery Guru or AccuBattery. You may use the app of your choice too, if your manufacturer does not provide an option to look at your battery’s health.
To expand the life and usability of our Android phone, we need to preserve the health of the battery. If not, we may have to replace the battery or the phone altogether. You can preserve the battery health on Android by following these simple tips.
Set a Custom Charging Limit
Android phones let us set a custom charging limit to preserve battery health and protect it from fast degradation of capacity. Manufacturers recommend setting the charging limit to 80- 90% and not beyond that. Charging our phone up to 100% every time is actually not recommended by manufacturers.
We always need to make sure our phone battery never falls below 10% or charges beyond 90%. You can set a custom charging limit in the Battery settings of your phone.
Open the Settings app on your phone and search for Battery health. Open the Battery health options. Toggle the button beside Custom charging limit. Then, set the limit as per the recommendations of the manufacturer.
These options may vary based on your phone manufacturer. The options remain the same, but the wording may change. Follow accordingly to set a custom charging limit.
After setting the custom charging limit, your phone will never charge beyond that percentage. If your manufacturer offers Smart Charging, Adaptive Charging, or Smart Charge options, you may even enable them to let them implement charging patterns based on your charging habits.
Use Chargers or Cables From Device Manufacturers
Charging phones with the available charger is bad for our device’s battery. We must get an adapter and cable made by the manufacturer to save the battery. If they are not available, we must ensure we get charging accessories that are compatible with our device from trusted brands.
Before getting a new charger for your phone, look at the specifications of your device and get the adapter and cable that support the power specified for your device.
Never Let Your Phone Overheat
Batteries degrade faster when they overheat or are exposed to heat. Do not expose your phone to direct sunlight or hot areas. Do not use your phone for heavy activities like gaming while it is charging.
Use Recommended Battery Settings
Phone manufacturers recommend certain settings to preserve battery health and extend its life. They can be found under the options provided in the Battery settings or the Battery optimization app provided by the manufacturer.
Follow those recommendations strictly to save your battery from degradation and faster draining.
Install Updates Regularly
It is not a wise choice to ignore installing pending updates. Android phones get monthly security updates and software updates regularly. We need to make sure they are installed automatically.
Fix a Fast-Draining Battery on Android
If you notice the battery of your Android phone is draining fast, you need to make sure there are no apps running in the background. Limit app activity in the background, update apps, turn off features that you do not use, install updates, and fix all the issues that are contributing to fast battery drain.

California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.
Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.
“The conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors,” said Bonta.
“Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors.”
The subpoena, issued on Thursday, followed Huang’s resignation a week ago after it emerged he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy.
Alice Huang, who is not related, is associated with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has bought nearly $5bn (£3.8bn) of Nvidia chips and hardware in recent years, and is being investigated for possibly diverting advanced restricted chips to China.
Megaspeed has said it is a “legitimate and lawful” business, and that Huang left the company late last year.
Bonta said the investigation would also look at whether the former Nvidia chief’s actions resulted in confidential information being passed to China.
“My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information,” he said. “And if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law.”
Nvidia’s shares are down by a fifth since Huang admitted the extramarital affair, hitting a one-year low at the close of trading on Thursday, and wiping almost $1tn off its market value.
Earlier this week, Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s chair, said the company had no intention of reinstating Huang after the former CEO said he would be “honoured” to return. Elon Musk and a host of tech bosses had campaigned for Nvidia to bring him back.
Huang is due to testify before several congressional committees over the potential breach of national security on 1 December.
Shares in rival chipmaker AMD closed down almost 8% on Thursday after the publication of reports connected to short seller Hunterbrook warning about its links to China and the “circular financing” of customers.
The company, which has been targeted amid the Nvidia scandal, is looking at a further fall of more than 5% in pre-market trading.
Hunterbrook Media published allegations on the use of AMD’s software by a Chinese server maker blacklisted by the US. Sister publication, The Bear Cave newsletter, alleged that AMD’s use of datacentre lease guarantees and backstops for unsold cloud computing capacity could leave it exposed to a pullback in AI spending.
AMD said the reports’ claims “misrepresent AMD’s business practices and relationships”.
“AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations,” the company said. “We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.”
AMD’s share price has more than doubled so far this year, giving the company a market capitalisation of more than $800m.

ED raids Keralam man for 4 hours in hawala case, then realises it was wrong house
The ED allegedly searched the wrong Naushad's house in Keralam while looking for another man linked to a suspected Rs 100-crore hawala transaction.
An Enforcement Directorate (ED) search in Keralam's Kozhikode district over an alleged Rs 100-crore hawala transaction took an unexpected turn when officials allegedly spent nearly four hours searching the wrong house, after mistaking its occupant for the person they were looking for.
The family alleged that they repeatedly told the officials that they had the wrong person, pointing out a mismatch in the father's name, but the search continued. Officials eventually showed them a photograph of the actual suspect towards the end of the operation, the family claimed.
The search was among those conducted at around a dozen locations across the state on Friday as part of an investigation into alleged foreign exchange violations and hawala transactions, officials said. The searches were carried out under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).
A family member said ED officials arrived at their house in Kozhikode district around 7 am and told them they were looking for a person named Naushad in connection with an alleged Rs 100-crore hawala transaction.
“When the ED officials said they were looking for the son of Usman, we told them that Naushad's father's name was Mohammed, not Usman. But the officials refused to leave. We allowed them to search the house. They completed the search but found nothing,” a family member told reporters, according to news agency PTI.
The family alleged that officials showed them a photograph of the person they were actually looking for only towards the end of the search. They said the person in the photograph was not the Naushad living at their house.
The search lasted nearly four hours. According to the family, Naushad had returned to Keralam around nine months ago after leaving his job at a company in Sharjah. He is currently working as a fisherman.
The family, along with the local ward member and other residents, alleged that the ED had mistaken Naushad's identity and demanded action against the officials. They said the agency should have verified the address and other identifying details before conducting the search.
There was no immediate response from ED officials to the family's allegation that the search was carried out because of mistaken identity.

Dozens missing after boat carrying 100 migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
- Published
Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a boat reportedly carrying about 100 migrants capsized off the coast.
Initial reports said that one person had died, but some local media have reported that at least four bodies have been recovered. Dozens of people are still missing.
Personal belongings were found on the badly damaged boat, which washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar. Search operations continued throughout Wednesday and were due to resume on Thursday.
This comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe killed at least 39 people, in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters.
Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, said the latest tragedy happened around 02:00 local time (02:00 GMT).
"Cries could be heard coming from the pirogue that were audible even from the beach," the AFP news agency quoted him as saying.
A survivor questioned by the police said there were about 100 people on the boat, including five women, AFP reported.
Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings from the wreckage, including a school enrolment document.
At a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about a renewed increase in irregular departure by migrants hoping to reach Europe.
He instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving the dangerous journeys and proposing measures to tackle the problem.
Following last month's tragedy, Faye had urged Senegalese people not to risk their lives attempting the dangerous sea crossings.
Many thousands of people from West Africa have died or gone missing trying to flee conflict, authoritarian rule or poverty in recent years.
The UN's migration agency IOM said last month that it had recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year alone.
It warned the figures were likely to be an underestimate, as many boats disappear without leaving survivors or a trace.
As it has become more difficult to reach Europe through North Africa, due to tighter controls and increased co-operation with European countries, migrants are increasingly targeting Spain's Canary Islands.
They often travel in wooden boats known as pirogues that are frequently overloaded and not suited to such long voyages across the Atlantic Ocean.
Most migrants arriving in the Canary Islands this year are from Senegal, according to the UN.
They are driven to leave home by limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks, according to the IOM.
On 7 November, El Hierro, one of the Canary Islands, declared a state of emergency following a surge in migrant arrivals.
It said more than 3,300 people had reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of the month. This amounts to almost a third of the island's population.
