Bengaluru-based NBFC InPrime Finserv has raised ₹101 Cr (about $10.7 Mn) in a Series B funding round led by Dutch entrepreneurial development bank FMO, with participation from existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures. The lender will use the capital to expand its geographical presence, enter the micro-mortgage segment, and strengthen its AI capabilities across underwriting and customer service. It also plans to increase investments in agentic AI and AI copilots. According to the NBFC, four in-house AI copilots currently support its credit team, while three AI-powered voice agents handled more than 1.26 Lakh customer calls between April and September 2026. Founded in 2021 by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj, and Rajat Singh, InPrime began operations in 2023. It lends to small business owners and self-employed individuals, including kirana store owners, dairy farmers, and beauty parlour operators — a customer group it calls the ‘informal prime’ segment. According to InPrime, these borrowers often run established businesses and own property but struggle to access formal credit, leaving them dependent on multiple lenders to meet their financing needs. “This funding will help us take that model further, expand our reach and use technology and AI to serve our customers better at scale,” cofounder Singh said. InPrime combines data-led underwriting with a field team to assess borrowers beyond conventional financial metrics. It said its AI systems help interpret unstructured data and support customer interactions in vernacular languages. It operates 46 area offices across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand, and Madhya Pradesh. It has served more than 27,000 households and disbursed ₹516.92 Cr in loans to date. As of September 30, 2026, its assets under management (AUM) stood at ₹332.8 Cr, while its gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio was 0.8%. The latest round takes InPrime’s total funding to ₹190 Cr. Its other investors include Info Edge Ventures, Kettleborough VC, and Titan Capital. The fundraise follows investments in other fintech companies with lending businesses. Olyv recently raised an additional $6 Mn from Nippon Life India AIF Management and existing investors in an extension of its Series B round. In August, global investment firm Prosus invested $100 Mn in Sachin Bansal-led fintech startup Navi, marking the latter's first institutional fundraise. The investment, which gives Prosus a minority stake in Navi, was cleared by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) last month.

Quick Answer
Nothing OS 5 brings a bunch of useful upgrades, from on-phone widget creation and new lockscreen clocks to split Quick Settings, Dual-View Video, easier iPhone sharing, the Glyph app, translucent themes, smarter QR scanning, and the new Geist font.
Nothing has updated all of its eligible devices to the latest version of its operating system, Nothing OS 5. It runs on top of Android 17, and in typical Nothing tradition, is clean and uncluttereds. And while it might seem broadly similar to its predecessor, there are a number of interesting new features – some important, some seemingly trivial – beneath that familiar surface. So if you have a Nothing phone and it has received the Nothing OS 5 update (there is a list of supported devices with rollout timelines here: https://in.nothing.tech/nothing-os), here are eleven things you must try out.
Table of Contents
Appy fizz: Now build snazzy widgets right on your phone, no coding experience required
One of the biggest innovations of the Nothing ecosystem was the introduction of Essential apps that let users, even with no coding knowledge, make widgets. In the past, you had to access Essential Apps on a computer to be able to make these widgets. Now you can do so right on your phone. And it is as easy as easy peasy apple squeezie. Mind you, you still need to sign up for Essential Apps and be part of a waiting list before you can get into design mode. No download is needed – the Essential Apps app comes to your Nothing phone when you update the phone to Nothing OS 5.g
Get a gooey or an info-loaded lockscreen clock!
On to the really serious stuff now. Perhaps the most noticeable visual change in NothingOS is the addition of two lockscreen clock widgets – Gooey and Micrographics. The Gooey clock has a bold and fluid look, with numbers looking a little melted. It is very eye-catching and, well, different. Those who want a truckload of information on their lockscreen and who opt for Micrographics get details like day, date, weather, temperature, upcoming appointments, and, of course, the time, all in rows that give it a very business ticker feel. This is how you clock into this feature:
- Long-press on the lock screen of your phone. This will show a Customize lock screen text bubble. Tap on it, and then tap on the fingerprint scanner to get into the Lock screen edit zone.
- Tap the clock widget space, which shows the time, and you will see Clock face options.
- Gooey is the second option, and right next to it is Micrographics. Choose the one you want, and also tweak its color as per your wish.
- Tap on Done, and hey, it’s, well…done.
Our own preference is the Micrographics widget, which is incredibly handy. We hope they add email and other notifications to it as well.
Split those notifications and quick settings
In the past – as on many phones – swiping down on a Nothing phone showed one new notifications, and swiping further down gave one access to Quick Settings (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Brightness, Torch, et al.). Well, you can split them into two separate zones if you wish. Once done, swiping from one side of the top will give you access to Quick Settings, while swiping from the other will show notifications. To do this segregation, just follow these steps:
- Open Settings and go to Notifications
- Go to the Notifications and Quick Settings Option
- You will see two options: Separate and Combined (classic).
- Select Separate, and now Notifications and Quick Settings will occupy different parts of the top panel.
Find out how long you have been away from your phone
One of the coolest new widgets on Nothing OS 5 is the Away Time widget, which lets you know how long you have kept away from your phone, and shows it in a simple, clean widget that can be placed on your home screen or your lock screen. It is a nice way to know about the “me time” you have given yourself away from your phone. Getting it is as easy as pressing on any place on the lock screen or Home Screen, and then selecting the Away Time widget option. We suggest going for the larger (4 x 2) one because it just looks so much better, especially with that zen-like blue background.
Keep what matters on the Home Screen – use Collector
Another widget (yes, Nothing seems to really like them widgets) that is very handy is Collector. You just open it and place images of what you want to keep seeing or consider important in it, and it automatically cuts out what it sees as important and keeps it handy on the home screen. It has a wonderful fridge sticker vibe, and keeps what matters close at hand. Just long-press on the home screen and select it from the widget collection!
Glyph Interface? There’s an app for that – finally!
The Glyph Interface has been one of the most eye-catching features of Nothing’s phones. This is basically a collection of LEDs on the back of the phones that light up in different patterns, showing notifications and battery levels, letting you know who is calling, controlling volume, setting timers, and doing more, all on the back of the phone. There was a catch, though. The Glyph UI had to be controlled from the settings of the phone, which seemed to be a rather roundabout way of doing things. This has now been fixed with the Glyph app, which gives one direct access to the Glyph Interface, letting one tweak it without having to get into the Settings. No downloads needed – the Glyph app appears on your Nothing phone the moment you update it to Nothing OS 5.
Lights, camera action…with both front and back cameras
Nothing OS 5 gives you the option to shoot videos using the rear as well as the front camera simultaneously. One can choose from having the footage one below the other, or having the selfie camera in an inset and the main camera in the larger part of the display. To access the option:
- Launch the Camera app
- Scroll across to More and choose Dual-View Video
It would have been nice to be able to take some stills with this feature, but as of now, it is limited to video.
There’s a glassy, classy “translucent” theme
Yep, your Nothing phone is now on the glass UI bandwagon. Mind you, this option is not turned on by default. You will need to follow these steps:
- Go to Settings, and then choose Customization
- Choose Theme & Style, and then choose Translucent. You can opt to have a dark theme in this if you wish.
- Honestly, it is not exactly eye-popping as of now. The translucence seems mainly to be around the widgets, and the app icons are not translucent. But it is a good starting point.
Scan that QR code, even if it wobbles
This is a pretty minor and yet handy change in Nothing OS 5. While camera icons have all been polished, a tiny yet useful tweak is in scanning QR codes, especially when using the scanner in crowded places or in slightly wobbly situations (think of paying in a moving vehicle). Now, when you use the camera to scan a QR code, the link it leads to remains on the screen, even if your hand moves and the QR code goes off or the code itself wobbles a little. So scanning codes is a whole lot easier, and you don’t have to bother about lining up the camera with the QR code all the time.
Send images to THAT friend with the iPhone easily (no app needed)
With Nothing OS 5, sending images to iPhones is pretty easy. Here’s how you do it:
- Ask your friend to switch on AirDrop on their iPhone and allow everyone to send images to it.
- Select the images you want to send on your Nothing phone.
- Select the Quick Share option, and then select the Use QR Code option.
- Scan the QR code with the iPhone’s camera. The images will be transferred.
Get the new font, Geist
Nothing’s marketing communications look very distinct because they use a font called Geist. Well, with NothingOS 5, you can now use Geist as the default font on their Nothing phones. This is how one does it:
- Head off to Settings again, and this time go to Display.
- Choose Font & Display Size.
- Once there, you can choose Geist as your default font.
- Once again, the difference is not going to jump out at you, but will become apparent as you use the phone.

A report published by Dainik Jagran newspaper is being shared on social media (here, here, here), claiming that Mayawati has announced her support for the BJP in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The report quotes Mayawati as saying, “Supporting the BJP in 2027 is the right decision for the stability, development and social harmony of the country and the state.” Let’s verify the claim made in the post. 
Claim: Dainik Jagran reported that BSP chief Mayawati would extend full support to the BJP in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
Fact: The alleged Dainik Jagran newspaper clipping is AI-generated. We could not find any such report in the newspaper’s 11 November 2026 e-paper editions or any announcement supporting the claim on Mayawati’s social media accounts. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A relevant keyword search did not yield any such report. The viral screenshot mentions 11 November 2026 as the publication date and identifies the day as Tuesday. However, 11 November 2026 was a Wednesday, raising suspicions about the screenshot’s authenticity. Further, we found no such report in any of the November 11 e-paper editions available on Dainik Jagran’s website. We also reviewed BSP supremo Mayawati’s Facebook and X accounts but found no posts supporting the viral claim.
To further verify its authenticity, we analysed the viral screenshot using various AI detection tools. OpenAI’s Verify tool and Sightengine AI both identified the newspaper clipping as likely AI-generated.
To sum up, the viral Dainik Jagran clipping claiming Mayawati’s support for the BJP in the 2027 UP elections is AI-generated.

The Congress party on Friday said it favoured resolving the issue of delimitation through consultations with all political parties, but accused the government of making no effort to engage the Opposition on the matter.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the party’s position was guided by a four-point formula: retaining the existing strength of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha; maintaining the present State-wise distribution of seats; reserving one-third (182) of the existing seats for women; and imposing a 25-year freeze on all three arrangements.
Mr. Ramesh said the need for an early consensus on the issue had become more pressing in view of of the fact that Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation would be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year.
This could be unfavourable to some southern states – which have made progress in population control – and hence not feasible, he added.
Mr. Ramesh said the Congress was not opposed to delimitation as such, but believed that the exercise should not place any State at a disadvantage.
The Congress leader claimed that all parties in the INDIA bloc, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), were on the same page on the four-point formula.
The DMK, he said, was also party to a resolution opposing any change in the number of Lok Sabha seats and seeking safeguards to ensure that Tamil Nadu was not disadvantaged by delimitation.
The Congress leader said seeking consultation was necessary because the government had not initiated any meaningful engagement with the Opposition.
He claimed that as per his information, the government has not shared a concrete proposal on delimitation even with constituents of the National Democratic Alliance.
The Congress wanted the matter to be discussed with all political parties and stakeholders to arrive at a consensus, Mr. Ramesh added.
The Monsoon session of Parliament has remained unprorogued since both Houses were adjourned sine die on August 13.
The decision has fuelled speculation about the possibility of the government convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional changes linked to women’s reservation and delimitation.
An extended or special sitting within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, while convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days’ notice.
Speculation also continues over the timing of the winter session. Parliament has not held a winter session on four occasions: in 1975, 1979, 1984 and 2020.

Peptides are poised to go mainstream with this week’s launches from telehealth companies Hims & Hers and Noom, both of which announced they will be offering prescriptions for eligible patients.
Synthetic peptides are a broad category of short-chain amino acids. Initially popular among bodybuilders, certain drugs in the class have gained traction among a broad swath of people looking to optimize their health — whether to build muscle, feel more energetic, increase libido, or recover from injuries. But many compounded peptides that are marketed to consumers are experimental. They have not been approved by the Food and Drug Administration, nor are there randomized controlled trials showing their safety and efficacy in humans. The Department of Health and Human Services, however, has foregrounded the drugs under health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an avowed peptide enthusiast.
While peptide prescriptions were already offered by smaller telehealth companies, Hims (with a market cap of more than $3.5 billion) and Noom (a private company valued at $3.7 billion) are two of the industry’s dominant players, making the announcements a pivotal moment for peptides in the United States.

A video (here & here) is being widely shared on social media, claiming to show police parading a man named Mohammad Junaid through the streets of Ujjain for allegedly extorting and threatening Hindu shopkeepers. Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: Video of Ujjain police parading a Muslim man named Mohammad Junaid through the streets for allegedly extorting money from Hindu shopkeepers.
Fact: The video shows police parading a person named Vijay alias Token, a Hindu, through the streets of Ujjain for attacking and threatening to extort money from local residents. Hence, the claim made in the post is False.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led to news reports (here, here & here) covering the incident. According to these reports, the video actually shows Ujjain police parading and thrashing a man named Vijay alias Token after he allegedly tried to extort money from locals.
On 21 October 2026, a local resident, Sona Solanki, lodged a complaint with the Panwasa police against Vijay and his associates. According to the FIR, the accused arrived outside Solanki’s house and demanded Rs 500 per month from the family to live in the neighbourhood. When the family refused to pay, the group attacked them and a neighbour who intervened.
Acting on the complaint, police arrested the main accused, 25-year-old Vijay alias Token, son of Gangaram Rathore and a resident of Talai Ki Pal in the Panwasa area. Police stated that Vijay is a habitual offender with 11 criminal cases registered against him between 2018 and 2026, including a previous arrest in an excise-related case. Following his arrest, police paraded him through the streets before he was remanded to judicial custody.
We contacted Shekhar Hariyala, the investigating officer at Panwasa Police Station, who was present during the parade. He confirmed that the man in the viral video is Vijay alias Token, a Hindu, and not Mohammad Junaid.
To sum it up, the viral video does not show police parading a Muslim man named Mohammad Junaid for extorting Hindu shopkeepers.

Culture, defence, Fernandes - Pochettino's priorities at Man Utd
- Published
"We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game."
Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.
The former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea boss wasted no time getting across the Atlantic Ocean after completing his stint in charge of the United States on Tuesday.
He met key staff on Wednesday, took training for the first time on Thursday and conducts his first wider media conference at United's Carrington training ground on Friday.
The 54-year-old is facing a packed schedule, starting with a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.
Pochettino accepted a big challenge. United are 18th in the table. By 17:00 GMT on Saturday, they could be bottom.
So, what are the Argentine's priorities as he begins the task of trying to transform United's season?
There is a clear non-negotiable.
"To create the culture is the most important [thing]," he told United's in-house media in a 15-minute introductory chat.
- Pochettino's first Man Utd training session filmed by drone operator 
  - Published1 hour ago
- Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino 
  - Published1 day ago
'Making the players feel like winners again'
It would be easy to point to areas of the pitch where United have been deficient this season. However, it cannot be totally dismissed that virtually the same group of players were transformed over the second half of last season by the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who guided them to third in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.
Remarkably, Pochettino has won twice as many matches in charge of the USA this season than the three victories United have managed, with a 100% record from six games.
United, by contrast, have not won in the Premier League since August, while two of their three victories have required the Red Devils to come from behind. Their single clean sheet came against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.
One of the most immediate tasks for Pochettino will be to alter the mindset of players who seem to have become restricted by the pressure they have found themselves subjected to.
"It is a mistake to see the situation," he said. "We need to see the potential of this club.
"We need to understand it is a game, and to connect with the game we need to feel free. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is our priority now; to work with them and take the pressure.
"Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back."
Fixing a leaky defence
That said, there are some glaring issues that Carrick was unable to fix and Pochettino must find an answer to. The most obvious is defence.
Who should the cornerstones of United's defence be?
The Carrick regime felt Leny Yoro was the player with the attributes - pace, strength and control - most suited to their needs. Yet, at 21, Yoro is prone to mistakes and he has also been needed at right-back because regular right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have, at times, been required on the left.
Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have not been reliable fitness wise. Pochettino knows the baggage attached to Martinez, given his post-match criticisms of the club hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, and the knowledge his fellow countryman's contract expires in the summer.
Harry Maguire has started all 10 league games this season but suffered a back spasm in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, immediately before the international break, and had to be replaced at half-time. Maguire has many attributes, but his presence does restrict the ability to press high up the field.
Ayden Heaven has made eight appearances in all competitions but has previously been regarded as being behind Yoro in terms of his overall development.
Then there is Dalot.
The 27-year-old was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee when he was replaced against Villa, such was the negative fan reaction to his performance, which included conceding a penalty at the start of the second-half.
It can justifiably be argued if Dalot has the talent to match the 260 club appearances he has now made.
However, for his faults, coaches love his attitude.
Dalot has been described to BBC Sport as having one of the most committed and professional approaches to the game, that he is someone willing to take responsibility, happy to play in unfamiliar positions if it benefits the team, the first to offer support to team-mates, and a positive influence in the dressing room.
Solving the Fernandes issue
Bruno Fernandes' alarming drop off in form has been one of the most noticeable features of the current campaign.
The Portugal playmaker has been a shadow of the star who scooped all the player of the year awards last season and broke the Premier League assist record.
He was axed for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League humiliation by Como and seems to be affected by concerns around his future - his contract also expires in the summer, although United are almost certain to trigger their one-year option on the 32-year-old - and the summer arrival of Youri Tielemans.
For the short term at least, Pochettino must decide whether to pick Fernandes in his favoured number 10 role and work around that, or drop him deeper, as Ruben Amorim did, or play him wide, which has not brought the best out of him.
What else? Can any youngsters step up?
Fernandes' status affects other areas. Carrick never seemed convinced by Andrey Santos, a £50m summer arrival from Chelsea. But with £70m Carlos Baleba out for an extended period, a partner needs to be found in midfield for Kobbie Mainoo.
Tielemans did not seem to have the running ability for the role, and Amorim wouldn't pick Mainoo with Fernandes.
Further forward, with Benjamin Sesko out, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have tended to be used in the number nine role. But Cunha likes to drop deep, while, after a bright start to the season, Mbeumo has scored twice in his past 12 appearances.
Neither Shea Lacey nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Both caught the eye on England Under-20 duty during the international break. Pochettino has history for giving young players a chance and the pair could benefit from that.
A united club?
There is one issue Pochettino mentioned in his interview he will soon discover requires delicate handling.
United's match-going fans have stood by every manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. There is no reason to think that will change now.
However, their relationship with the club's ownership is fractured, possibly beyond repair. Fresh accounts to 30 September show the club's overall debt remains more than £1.1bn and a further £14.5m was spent on finance costs in the previous quarter.
This fuels discontent in the stands, already heightened because of various ticketing measures, none of which are viewed by most supporters as being positive.
"We need to be united," said Pochettino.
"Chemistry is really important, chemistry between us and the staff and the fans and the players, the directors, the owners and everything."

The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
BRUSSELS — A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences, and just perhaps, to pave the way for them to get back together.
Burnham is scheduled to hold just under an hour of talks in Brussels with European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Then they'll all meet in a plenary session with U.K. government ministers and European commissioners.
Burnham has described the rare EU-U.K. summit — only the second since Britain became the first country to leave the world's biggest trading bloc — as a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce.
"The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we gained," he said this week.
Burnham has said all options should be on the table for future relations, including rejoining the now-27-nation bloc. But he's stressed that reversing Brexit is just one possible outcome, and far from imminent. It would need the backing not just of British voters, but the unanimous support of a mistrustful EU. Still, he has broken a long political code of silence on the option of rejoining.
Ahead of the meeting, von der Leyen said she wanted it to be "a summit of ambition and concrete results. More opportunities for young people. Easier agrifood trade. And a stronger cooperation on economic security."
Burnham pitched the package of agreements expected to be signed Friday as a way of "cutting costs, keeping prices down in the supermarkets and creating opportunities for young people."
He said "a closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe."
The deals are set to include an agreement for up to 100,000 young adults from Britain to live and work in EU countries for up to three years, and the same number of Europeans to come to the U.K.
There will also be an emissions trading agreement and a deal to remove checks on food and agricultural products that will make things cheaper and easier for British exporters to Europe. Burnham says the deals could add a modest 0.4% to Britain's economy.
To get the deals, the U.K. must accept some EU rules and standards that it has no role in setting. Supporters of Brexit say that undermines Britain's independence.
"I'm afraid that the great Brexit debate has just started again," Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told the BBC. He said "it's perfectly clear that this very, very soon becomes a debate about: do we rejoin or do we stay out?"
The war in Ukraine, and the U.K.'s military strength, are drawing the two back together, and the summit provides the EU with an opportunity to discuss stronger cooperation on security and defense, as well as efforts to restrict irregular migration.
"Our security and prosperity are closely intertwined, making a strong partnership between us essential," Costa said ahead of the meeting. "By deepening our cooperation, we can strengthen our ability to address the challenges of our time, strengthen our resilience and promote stability in Europe and beyond."
Nevertheless, feelings remain raw, and EU officials have been reluctant to encourage talk of the U.K. rejoining. They are weary from the shifting demands of seven British prime ministers over the last decade and want real clarity about the country's intentions.
Ireland's ambassador in London, Sonja Hyland, said that when Britain voted for Brexit, "there was a lack of clarity as to exactly what that meant." If Britain wants to reopen negotiations, she said, it must "make a clear decision as to what it wants."

Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
SHENZHEN, China and MOSCOW, Russia — President Trump joined Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China on Thursday – capping two days of talks characterized by high-minded tributes to the role of great powers in maintaining peace, even as the men who led them had a role in starting some of the most intractable conflicts around the globe.
"History tells us when great powers are at peace, the world is secure," said Xi in opening remarks before cameras. "When great powers clash, the world is in chaos."
Putin noted their nations could make a "significant contribution to strengthening security and stability in the world."
"In that sense and I think in lots of other ways, we are making history," said Trump, who called it a "special responsibility" for the three countries to work together.
Yet, they offered few solutions toward peace, with the leaders offering divergent agendas going in:
Trump wanted to talk about reducing nuclear weapons and his mission to keep Iran from obtaining them; Putin was looking to push for an end to the war in Ukraine on terms favorable to Moscow; Xi was signaling he hoped to avoid wading too deep into either topic — preferring to showcase China's growing global clout with more general statements promoting peace and economic stability.
There were also topics to avoid: Trump refused to engage with journalists' questions over China's alleged role in an espionage plot to steal high end Nvidia chips.
In the end, the summit's key deliverable was arguably the image itself: the president of the United States gathering with authoritarian leaders from China and Russia for the first time in American history.
Summit speed dating
Despite being billed as a summit of "groundbreaking significance" by the Chinese hosts, sit-down talks between Trump, Xi, and Putin were relatively brief — with some of that time taken up by interpreters delivering simultaneous translation.
Trump's meeting with Putin lasted 42 minutes. His talks with Xi went about an hour. The trilateral group session went on for an hour and a half.
Still, it was enough time for familiar Trump bonhomie to emerge.
"Who's he? He's my friend," said a smiling Trump upon seeing Putin ahead of their bilateral meeting.
"We've known each other for a long time," added Trump after he and the Russian leader warmly shook hands. "And I think a lot of wonderful things can come of this. Or at least start."
Similarly, Trump told Xi "as long as you and I are in charge of things, we're never going to have a problem."
Both statements were tacit admissions the clock is ticking on Trump's remaining two years in office — with change coming even sooner to Washington when Democrats take control of Congress come January.
Getting there
The China gathering was first proposed by Putin during an October phone call with Trump — an offer to meet together with President Xi when China hosted the Asian Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference in China that November.
For Putin in particular, the meeting was always going to be a coup: the latest sign that — with Trump and Xi's help — he has effectively chipped away at Western attempts to isolate him politically over his invasion of Ukraine.
Back in Moscow, state media showed footage of the three leaders huddled together seemingly on loop — proof that Russia had regained what the Kremlin sees as its rightful place among global superpowers.
Ignored by Kremlin-friendly media were hints at more subtle power dynamics at play.
Xi greeted Trump on the tarmac personally — returning a gesture Trump had given the Chinese leader during his recent visit in Washington — while Putin received a more scaled down delegation upon arrival to Shenzhen.
Similarly, Trump was offered the top spot next to Xi during the APEC group photo and sat next to Xi during the APEC dinner reception — with Putin positioned at a separate table.
Was it a slight to Putin? A calculated attempt to flatter Trump? A reflection of Russia's vastly weaker economy? Whatever the answer, Xi wasn't ignoring his Russian guest entirely.
The two gathered privately for two hours on Wednesday — a sit-down China-Russia watchers estimated to be their 50th meeting all told.
Xi and Putin also echoed each other in their public speeches— both touching on familiar themes of the dawn of a new "multipolar world" and criticizing the use of sanctions as a sign of Western influence on the wane.
A new Yalta?
From the outset, critics of the summit voiced concern that Trump, Xi, and Putin would seek to carve the world into each country's perceived sphere of influence.
In Russia, the event was billed as a potential "new Yalta" — a reference to a moment in 1945 when the leaders of the U.S., Soviet Union, and United Kingdom hastily agreed to a post-World War II order for Europe.
Instead, the Shenzhen summit reflected the far more fragmented priorities of its participants.
Trump made no secret he hoped to include China in arms control talks — what Trump calls "denuclearization" — at a moment when key landmark nuclear treaties between Russia and the U.S. have all expired.
The catch: his Chinese hosts had little interest in the issue.
Beijing has repeatedly rebuffed U.S. attempts to include it in negotiations with Russia — noting that its arsenal remains far below those of Cold War-era rivals Moscow and Washington.
Differences also extended to the war in Ukraine, where Putin had hoped to press for U.S. and Chinese support for a settlement tilted in Moscow's favor — including a redrawn security map for Europe that would amount to a rollback of NATO from Eastern Europe.
Xi has insisted Europe have a seat at the table in any negotiated settlement. Trump has largely relied on his trusted envoys — real estate developer Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner — to hash out the complexities of any peace deal.
Following Trump's meeting with Putin, a Kremlin aide would only say that Ukraine had been the focus of the discussions — adding the Kremlin leader had left "in an excellent mood."
It was hard to see why.
Just hours earlier, Ukraine carried out a missile strike on the lone bridge linking mainland Russia to the annexed Crimean peninsula for the third time this week — effectively disabling the structure for months to come.
The bridge is widely considered the Russian leader's pet project — a symbol of Russia's claim to territory illegally seized from Ukraine in 2014 rendered in steel.

Four babies who died in New South Wales – three after free births and one after a home birth – might have survived if they had had routine checks and follow-up , a coronial inquest has heard.
Baby DH, Baby D, Baby R, and Baby B died in the state’s northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024.
The inquest in Lismore has heard women chose free or home births for reasons including traumatic experiences, a lack of trust in clinicians, and a lack of services.
Baby DH died about eight hours after he was born in a free birth – with a doula but no medical professionals present. The court earlier heard he turned purple, was struggling to breathe and had became floppy.
His parents gave evidence they were worried but the doula kept reassuring them their baby was OK, then left.
The doula denied many of their claims, and denied that she gave them any clinical advice.
Expert neonatologist and associate professor Nicholas Evans said on Friday that Baby DH’s complex heart abnormalities “would have been readily detectable” in a routine pregnancy scan after which he would have been referred to a paediatric cardiologist.
It was a “missed opportunity”, he told the court.
Paediatric cardiologist Dr Paul Brooks said it was “highly likely” all the abnormalities would have been identified in a routine scan before birth.
Even if the extent of the abnormalities wasn’t clear, he told the court, the scan would have shown the baby needed to be born at a major hospital with cardiac surgery capabilities.
“The site of [Baby DH’s] birth meant that he didn’t have a chance.”
Baby D’s mother did not know she was having twins, and at first thought she’d delivered Baby D’s placenta, only to realise it was a stillborn second twin.
Experts at the inquest agreed it was impossible to know exactly why Baby D died. They discussed the possibility it was because self-described birth keeper Sita Tara Kali did not clamp the umbilical cord before cutting it, but Evans told the court that it was ultimately most likely from respiratory distress because of his compromised heart function.
Baby D might have survived if someone who could do advanced resuscitation had arrived in under 10 minutes, he said, but the “root cause” was that it was not known the mother was carrying twins before the births.
“If [twins] had been diagnosed, at 18 weeks, as it would usually in pregnancy, there would have been very close monitoring.”
Baby R likely died of “severe post-maturity” after being born at 43 weeks and one day in a free birth. The standard is to induce birth or perform a caesarean section at 42 weeks, as the ageing placenta puts the baby at risk.
The mother had been for an ultrasound at 12 weeks, which had put the date of birth at 28 July, 2020.
But the mother distrusted hospitals and trusted Kali, her birth keeper, the court previously heard.
Kali told her to calculate her due date from the date of conception, an unreliable measure that put the date of birth in mid-August.
That recalculation, Evans wrote in his report to the court, was the “root cause” of the issue.
“The standard practice now is that you don’t allow a pregnancy to go beyond 42 completed weeks,” Evans said on Friday.
Expert midwives earlier told the court they didn’t have statistics for babies born beyond 43 weeks because it was so rare.
A 19 August ultrasound showed the pregnancy had become a medical emergency – but Kali advised her to “go home and rest”. It is “more likely than not” that the baby would have survived had she gone to hospital after the ultrasound, Evans said.
Baby B’s mother was warned multiple times she needed to go to hospital to give birth to her twins, but she was determined to have a home birth. Rather than let her have a free birth, four midwives assisted her and the head midwife repeatedly counselled her about the risks.
The mother declined ultrasounds as well as a test for early onset group B streptococcus (GBS) – an organism present in 15 to 20% of women that infects the babies of about 2% of carriers.
Baby B likely died of GBS, pneumonia and sepsis, Evans told the court on Friday, while his twin fell ill but survived. Many infected babies survive in hospital thanks to antibiotics, he added.
The inquest is ongoing.

Nuvera has joined Polygon’s Open Money Stack (OMS). With this, the US-based payments infrastructure provider will leverage the L2 blockchain startup’s stack to enable stablecoin settlement for cross-border payments. Simply put, the blockchain startup will help Nuvera’s users initiate standard bank transfers even though funds will move onward in stablecoins. Nuvera’s integration with Open Money Stack (OMS) is aimed at addressing delays in international wire transfers. Traditional cross-border wire transfers rely on correspondent banking networks, which frequently introduce multi-day delays and opacity around fund locations due to strict banking cut-off hours. With OMS, Nuvera’s clients can continue paying via familiar local banking rails or SWIFT into a Nuvera-issued dollar account. Once the funds land, the corpus converts into stablecoins and settles immediately across supported networks. “Big things ahead for the Nuvera team. Excited to see them live on Polygon Open Money Stack, using stablecoins to keep settlement moving outside banking hours for their customers,” said Polygon cofounder Sandeep Nailwal. Founded in 2014 by Nailwal, Jaynti Kanani, Anurag Arjun, and Mihailo Bjelic, Polygon earned its fame as a low-cost blockchain network. The startup is now evolving into a full-stack payments infrastructure company. At the core of Polygon’s new identity is its Open Money Stack – a suite of payments tools designed to help businesses move money across bank accounts, cards, cash and stablecoin wallets via a single system. Instead of stitching together separate third-party providers for each step of a transaction, Open Money Stack enables businesses to oversee payment flows and manage fund movement from a unified dashboard. The startup claims that its architecture accepts cash and debit cards and disburses funds to bank accounts, cash pickup locations, and blockchain wallets across Polygon, Ethereum, and Solana. It also supports the x402 protocol, which enables AI agents to autonomously execute payments in USDC within pre-authorised spending limits. This comes as Polygon continues to tap into acquisitions to pick up fintech licences and close compliance gaps. Earlier this year, it acquired US-based crypto platforms Coinme and Sequence for around $250 Mn, enabling the company to become regulated under a money transmitter licence. The company is also planning to undertake multiple acquisitions of around $50-100 Mn each in order to acquire the required licences across various regions globally, cofounder Nailwal told Moneycontrol recently. It is already in the process of acquiring another US company, he added.

The Best Theraguns and Therabody Devices for Rest and Relaxation
Featured in this article
Theraguns are the gold standard for massage guns, so much so that the name has become synonymous with the category. But Therabody, the innovative company behind Theragun, has expanded its repertoire to boost wellness for more than just sore muscles and pain relief. It now offers a suite of gadgets to alleviate eye strain, soothe menstrual cramps, and depuff your skin (to name a few). We haven't tried every product in their lineup—we're getting there—but we've put several to the test, and these are our favorites. Plus, most of these gadgets are FSA/HSA eligible and designed with USB-C charging.
While Theraguns are an excellent investment for active individuals, it's worth noting that percussive massage guns are available at lower price points. If you're not married to the Therabody brand, see our Best Massage Guns for alternative recommendations that won't break the bank.
Updated March 2026: I've added the Theragun Mini Plus, the JetBoots Pro Plus, the SleepMask, and the TheraFace Mask Glo as new favorites. I updated the Honorable Mentions section with more products. Prices and links were also updated.
Honorable Mentions
TheraFace Mask for $650: The TheraFace Mask is a cordless, hands-free light-therapy device that uses three wavelengths (red, infrared, and blue) to tackle different skin care needs. To distinguish itself from its competitors, the TheraFace Mask includes a built-in vibration therapy mode that massages pressure points around the eyes, brow line, and scalp for some added stress relief. It comes with removable eye shields and a sleek display stand, which makes it easy to store on your nightstand.
JetBoots Prime for $550: Compared to the JetBoots Pro Plus, the JetBoots Prime keeps it simple: You get four pressure levels (25, 50, 75, and 100 mmHg) and three durations (20, 40, or 60 minutes), all adjustable throughout your session through a built-in control panel. They’re wireless with a 180-minute battery life and can even be used while charging. Plus, they fold down into the included drawstring bag, making them portable and fuss-free to stow away.
WaveRoller for $180: Foam rollers are great for improving range of motion, increasing blood flow, and reducing muscle tension. You can buy a decent foam roller for significantly less, but the WaveRoller offers Therabody app integration for a personalized experience and five vibration frequencies. Designed for full-body use, it works best for warm-ups and post-workout recovery.
TheraFace Pro for $420: The TheraFace Pro includes six detachable magnetic heads for cleansing, microcurrent, percussive massage, and LED light therapy—blue light for acne, red light, and infrared for anti-aging. Former reviewer Haley Sprankle tested the facial device and said her skin was softer and brighter, but she also noted that no clinical studies prove that microcurrent is an effective facial treatment.
Theragun Mini (3rd Generation) for $220: I recommend the Mini if you’re new to percussive therapy or need something packable for travel. It's the smallest and lightest Theragun, with three attachments (standard ball, dampener, and thumb) and a soft-zip case that fits into a tote, gym bag, or carry-on.
Theragun Sense for $300: The Theragun Sense is slightly smaller (and lighter) than the Pro Plus, and it’s also impressively quiet. Some settings are almost silent, allowing for a discreet recovery session at whatever time of day without having to worry about bothering your housemates. It has the same LCD screen and breathwork features as the Pro Plus, too. The main difference here is that it's compatible with fewer attachments, but four heads are still more than enough for the active individual.
Theragun Pro (5th Generation) for $530: Therabody still sells a few older generations as well as refurbished models directly. You may find even older models for sale on Amazon. While we haven't tried them all, we think it comes down to price. Anything older than 2019 or 2020 releases might not be worth it unless the price is shockingly low. This Pro came out in 2022, so it's still a decent deep tissue massager. If you can find it on sale and don't need all the latest updates, you should be happy with this one over the Pro Plus.
What Am I Testing Next?
I'll be testing the Theragun Prime (6th Generation) for $330, the RecoveryTherm Cube for $160, and the RecoveryPulse Arm for $160.

This week was a Skydance buyout deadline for employees to decide whether to accept a buyout offer, including at CBS News.
The offer came following the closing of Skydance’s purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as the company seeks $6 billion in savings. The merger puts CBS News and CNN under the same corporate umbrella.
At CBS News, the buyout was accepted by employees across the news division, with the London bureau among the most impacted, sources familiar with the plans said. Some staffers on 60 Minutes also took the buyout, although none were in key lead editorial roles, according to a source.
In the Washington bureau, Mary Hager, senior executive producer of Face the Nation, announced her departure earlier this month after 35 years at the network, although CBS News did not say whether her exit was tied to the buyout offer. Anne Hsu, who has been executive producer, is moving to the network’s Hong Kong bureau.
Watch on Deadline
All told, less than 10% of staffers offered buyouts accepted them, according to a source. In its report on the buyouts, Status newsletter reported that dozens took the offer, including producers and members of the operational staff in London. The UK’s labor laws also require robust offers compared to the U.S., while there also has been some anxiety over the future with two major news brands under the same ownership.
While CNN and CBS News remain as separate news entities, media companies looking to cut costs often look to foreign bureaus for savings. And this week, Skydance CEO David Ellison said that while he’s “incredibly happy” operating CNN and CBS News as they are, there “might be some news sharing” in the future.
CNN’s buyout deadline was earlier this month.
CBS News went through a round of cuts last October and another round in March. The latest round represented about 6% of the workforce, or around 60 to 70 employees out of about 1,100.

Step 1: Open Terminal and type the command: claude –version, and press Return. If you see a version number, it means Claude Code is already installed on your device. You can skip to Part 2 to continue setup.
If you see something like zsh: command not found: claude, it means Claude Code is not installed on your device, or Terminal can not find it yet. Follow the next steps to install Claude Code on your Mac.
Install Claude Code: To install Claude Code, use the official Anthropic installer. To do that, open Terminal on your Mac and paste this command: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Wait a few minutes, and then you will see a ” Claude Code successfully installed message in your terminal.
Check the setup notes below. If you see something like installation exists but ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH, it means the terminal still can’t find Claude Code yet.
Now follow the next two steps. If you don’t see such a note, you can quit the terminal, reopen it, and use this command to confirm that Claude Code has been successfully installed on your device: confirm claude –version. If you see a Claude version, it’s installed on your device. Then continue with part two.
Next, paste this command into the terminal and press Enter: echo ‘export PATH=”$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH”‘ >> ~/.zshrc
Next, paste this: source ~/.zshrc, and press Enter. Now type claude –version and press Enter. You will see the Claude version number. This means Claude Code is successfully installed on your device in the terminal
Part 2: Turn on Claude access in Edits
Next, you need to let Claude access your Instagram edits apps. First, ensure the Instagram edits app is installed on your Mac. If not, you can use the official download link here. Once installed, follow the steps below:
Step 1: Open the app on your Mac and sign in with your account. On the home screen, you will go directly to the Projects tab.
Step 2: Next, you can tap on your profile picture in the top right corner of the screen or click on the edit option in the menu bar at the top of the screen and then click on the settings
Step 3: Next, tap on the automation from the sidebar
Step 4: By default, automation is turned off. Now, from the automation settings, turn on the toggle that says Enable Automation Server.
Step 5: Under the Connect an AI Client section, click the copy icon next to the Claude code. This will copy the connection command with your access token. Remember, don’t share this command with others. In this case, I am using Claude code. If you are using Codex, tap the copy button next to Codex. The same goes for Muse.
You can also connect any AI model. Since it is a standard MCP server, any AI app can connect to the MCP server over HTTPS and can control edits.
Remember to replace <TOKEN> with the Access token from Edits > Settings > Automation, and keep Edits open with the automation server turned on
For Google Gemini CLI:
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For Qwen:
npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code
qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp

}
}
}
}
Part 3: Connect Claude Code to Edits
Next, let’s connect Claude Code (or any AI model) to edits. Remember that you can only do this once.
Step 1: Now, paste the command you copied from the previous section into the terminal. You will see: Added HTTP MCP server metapilot-native
Step 2: Next, for Claude, paste this command: claude mcp get metapilot-native and press Enter. Under status, if you see Connected, it worked. If it says Failed to connect, ensure the edits app is running and follow the previous steps carefully.
For other models, follow these:
| App (models) | Connect command | Check it worked | 
| Claude Code (Claude) | claude mcp add –transport http –scope user metapilot-native http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” | claude mcp get metapilot-native | 
| Gemini CLI (Gemini) | gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | gemini mcp list | 
| Qwen Code (Qwen) | qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | qwen mcp list | 
| Codex (OpenAI GPT) | echo ‘export EDITS_TOKEN=”<TOKEN>”‘ >> ~/.zshrc && source ~/.zshrc && codex mcp add edits –url http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –bearer-token-env-var EDITS_TOKEN | Run codex, then type /mcp | 
| OpenCode (DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM and more) | No command. Paste the opencode.jsonc block from my last message into the folder you run OpenCode in. | opencode mcp list |

Part 4: Start Claude Code
Now go to the folder where the videos are saved to edit them using Instagram edits. I recommend that you store all the videos in the Movies folder so it is easy to access in the future. In this case, I stored all my files in the Movies folder on my Mac. Now, once you have access to the folder, follow the steps below.
Step 1: To use Claude, go to the folder using the CD command. For example: cd ~/Downloads or cd ~/Movies. In my case, cd ~/Movies. Next, once you are in the folder, Type Cluade and press Return.
Step 2: Claude will ask whether you trust the folder you provided. Use the down arrow and select I trust this folder, and press Enter. It asks only once, and once you give permission, you can store all future videos in this folder for edits.
Step 3: To check, you can type /mcp and press Enter. It lists the apps Claude Code is connected to. metapilot-native with a green tick means Claude can control Edits.
Step 4: Go to the metapilot-native option and press Enter to see more details. You can use the down or up arrow to navigate between the options.
Part 5: Make your first Reel with Claude
Now let’s use Claude to create my first reel. In this case, I asked Claude to edit a 50-second coffee reel from five clips. In your case, you can store all the clips in the folder. First, test the connection again. Once done, follow the steps below.
To test the connection, go to your folder and type list my Instagram edits projects and press Enter. You will see metabolist native and the table of all your edit projects.
Step 2 : Now you can ask Claude to make edits for the Instagram reel video. You can manually create a new project, add clips, and point Claude to the project title and edit your videos, or you can ask Claude to create a project, add clips, and edit your first reel. I recommend giving Claude the full location of your clips and the title.
Step 3: That’s it. Claude will now create a new project and add Sunclips. You can open the Instagram Edits app to see the changes.
Step 4: Once you’ve loaded the clips, you can ask Claude to add transitions between them and also add titles, sound effects, and much more. In this case, I’m asking Claude to add the title “Morning Coffee” in big white text for two seconds and then add smooth transitions between the clips.
Step 5: Once you’ve made the edits, you can also ask Claude Core to export the clips in 4K, and it does it for you.
Step 6: Once the video is exported, Claude notifies you of the length, format, and size. You can open the same folder to see the clip. Claude also notifies you where the clip is stored and its title.
Let AI Handle Your Video Editing
This is how to connect Claude code using Instagram Edits MCP. For now, the Instagram Edits app is only available on macOS, and you can connect any AI model to make edits.
Since Claude requires a subscription, you can try a free AI model if you have one. You can also run any free AI model locally and ask it to edit, but the quality may vary and may not be as good as frontend models.
Since this guide focuses entirely on Claude Code, we are also creating a separate guide on how to connect other free AI models, including Google Gemini (which comes with a free Jio AI offer), DeepSeek, and other models.
If you have any issues while connecting Claude Code, let me know. If you prefer a video guide, we have also created one that you can check out above.

Kyiv’s mayor said Russian missiles killed three people, injured 15 and damaged three of the capital’s bridges over the Dnipro river overnight into Friday.
Vitali Klitschko added that a fire broke out in a three-story building in northern Kyiv as the city was pounded by multiple waves of missiles.
The overnight strikes, the largest on routes connecting the left and right banks of Kyiv since the start of the war, came hours after Vladimir Putin told Ukraine to expect a "painful" retaliation for its successful strikes this week on his flagship £3bn bridge to occupied Crimea.
Putin made the threat after an unprecedented trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Donald Trump which ended without any breakthroughs on the wars in either Ukraine or Iran.
While Trump opened the gathering by declaring the trio were “really making history,” the talks concluded with a four-point “peace declaration” that made no mention of either Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine or Washington’s conflict with Iran.
European leaders, who were excluded from the Shenzhen talks, warned that the warm reception afforded to Putin would only embolden the Kremlin to escalate its campaign against Ukraine.
Troops from 11 European nations drill in Poland for postwar Ukraine mission
Thousands of European troops are taking part in an unprecedented military exercise in southeastern Poland to prepare for a potential postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilise the country and rebuild its military once the war ends.
Led by France and the UK, the multinational force is a non-Nato military initiative of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, a wider political group of 37 nations supporting Ukraine.
The two-week exercise that began on 9 November is for the first time checking the coalition's ability to deploy in Ukraine after the war. It is aimed both at testing deployment plans and sending a message to Russia and the Donald Trump administration that European countries are stepping up militarily.
The exercise took place as leaders from Ukraine and nearly 40 other delegations met in Berlin, Germany, to underline their support for Kyiv and explore Ukraine’s postwar security arrangements. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants to ensure that Russia doesn’t invade again, while Moscow wants to keep the Nato military alliance away from its borders.
Rival summit on Ukraine pushes for European role in talks to end war
European leaders have expressed their readiness to negotiate with Russia to end the war in Ukraine, insisting that Europe must have a seat at the table.
Speaking at the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, British prime minister Andy Burnham said Europe had a “united negotiating position”, while German chancellor Friedrich Merz argued Russia’s “maximalist demands” were unrealistic.
“The US understands that there can be no peace without us. We, in turn, know that with the United States by our side, the prospects for peace increase,” Mr Merz added.
US envoy Jared Kushner said Donald Trump wanted to reach a deal with Europe’s support, adding that the president believed “peace is achievable” following his meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin and Chinese president Xi Jinping at the Apec summit in Shenzhen.
Mr Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff travelled to Berlin to brief some 40 European leaders on Mr Trump’s efforts to end the nearly five-year war following his historic trilateral talks with Mr Putin and Mr Xi this week.

Ukrainian attack kills three in Russian-held Luhansk
Three people were killed in a Ukrainian attack in Russian-controlled Luhansk, local authorities said on Friday.
A Ukrainian drone attack, meanwhile, damaged an industrial facility in Russia's western region of Smolensk, governor Vasily Anokhin said on Friday, without identifying it.
No air threat following suspected airspace breach, Polish PM says
Donald Tusk said on Friday he had received reports from ministers regarding the violation of Polish airspace and that there was currently no threat from the air.
"Appropriate services are operating on site," Tusk wrote on X.
Attacks on Thursday killed four civilians in Russia and two in Ukraine, officials say
The Russian defence Ministry said yesterday that its defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.
A Ukrainian attack on Russia’s Saratov region killed three people and wounded two others, local governor Roman Busargin said, and a drone killed a woman traveling by bicycle with her 8-year-old grandson in the Bryansk region, governor Egor Kovalchuk said.
Ukrainian authorities said that Russia launched anti-ship missiles and 98 drones at Ukraine, with hits recorded at 18 locations. Explosions and sirens rang out across Kyiv during the day, and the Dutch and Austrian embassies sustained minor damage, officials said.
Two people, including a 44-year-old woman, were killed and at least 23 people, including a 12-year-old boy, were reported wounded as Russian strikes caused damage in 12 regions.
Russia’s bigger army hopes to exhaust Ukraine on the front line through sheer weight of numbers in terms of soldiers, armour and weapons. But Kyiv’s defences are largely holding the Russians back, sapping Russian momentum with the help of drones that quickly choke off troop advances.
Russia has resorted to strategic bombing to wear down Ukraine’s resistance, placing special emphasis on knocking out power ahead of winter, while Kyiv’s domestically developed long-range drones and missiles have struck deep inside Russia, often targeting its oil refineries.
Polish airport suspends flights as military aircraft scramble
Poland’s Rzeszow airport suspended flight operations due to the activation of military aircraft, the Polish Air Navigation Services Agency said.
The Polish Air Force was conducting preventive operations related to Russian missile attacks on Ukraine, the Polish army said in a post on Friday.
Russia strikes sea vessels, energy infrastructure and transport facilities in Ukraine
Russia's defence ministry said on Friday its forces hit defence industry facilities as well as energy and transport infrastructure in several regions of Ukraine, including the capital Kyiv.
Also hit were port infrastructure facilities in the Odessa region and sea vessels used for Ukrainian military purposes, the ministry added.
Three killed in largest Russian attack on bridges in Kyiv
A Russian ballistic missile attack hit three bridges on Kyiv's Dnipro river and killed three people, the city's mayor said on Friday. It was the biggest attack on routes connecting the left and right banks of Ukraine's capital since the start of the war.
The missiles hit the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Pivdennyi bridges, Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram, resulting in closure or traffic restrictions in the city of some 3 million people commuting over six main bridges.
Three people were killed and 15 injured, he added. The strikes, which also caused fires and damaged critical infrastructure and buildings, came after Russian president Vladimir Putin promised to hit back hard in retaliation for Ukraine hitting the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week.
The strikes follow warnings from European allies on Thursday against any attempt to decide a peace settlement over their heads, after US president Donald Trump embraced Putin as a "friend" at a summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
Trump signals support for security guarantees for Ukraine
The summit between European leaders in Berlin on Thursday was called to discuss postwar security arrangements for Ukraine. President Volodymyr Zelensky wants to ensure that Russia doesn’t invade again, while Moscow wants to keep the Nato military alliance away from its borders.
“I think we’ve gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5,” US envoy Jared Kushner said. “And I think that that comes with at least what the Russians are saying, which is their intention is when this war is over to not have another war in the future.”
Kushner said Trump is “open” to an Article 5-like security guarantee for Ukraine, although “obviously it has to be in America’s interest to do that. And we also have to make sure that it’s part of a broader security package.”
He stressed that Trump wants to make a deal with Europe “by his side,” and is not looking to impose a unilateral agreement.
"Any deal we do will be in close consultation with Ukraine and with Europe. And that’s something that he also asked us to come here today and reassure people in that regard,” said Kushner, who is Trump's son-in-law.
He and Witkoff have led Trump administration efforts to end the war that followed Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine. The most recent talks in Abu Dhabi last week yielded no major breakthrough.
Trump called into the Berlin talks following his meeting with Putin. He is said to have lamented the amount being spent on the war, though there were conflicting reports about the tone of his remarks.

GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
Sen. Ron Johnson on efforts to avert government shutdown during lame duck session
Republican Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, who has defended President Trump's war with Iran, said Friday that he opposes tying government funding to an end to the conflict as Congress struggles to avert a shutdown before Christmas.
"We're not going to shut down the war. That is President Trump's power. He's exercising his constitutional authority," Johnson, who chairs the Senate Budget Committee, told Morning Edition.
Congress faces a Dec. 11 deadline to keep federal agencies operating, giving Democrats leverage in the Republican-controlled Senate, where most legislation requires 60 votes to advance. But both parties face divisions. Democrats disagree over whether to use the funding deadline to force an end to the war, while Republicans are weighing bipartisan negotiations against a party-line approach to securing additional military spending.
Johnson said Republicans would prefer to negotiate a spending agreement with Democrats rather than use budget reconciliation, a procedure that could allow them to approve defense funding without Democratic support.
"I think we'll give them one more chance," he said, referring to negotiations before the Thanksgiving recess.
Johnson, who previously supported military aid to Ukraine but later opposed additional funding, warned that temporary spending measures would hinder military modernization and weapons procurement. He pointed to the changing nature of warfare in Ukraine as an example.
A shutdown could furlough hundreds of thousands of federal workers or delay their pay just weeks before Christmas. Johnson said he hoped to avoid one but warned that Republicans would need Democratic support.
The war launched by the U.S. and Israel against Iran has killed thousands of people, threatened U.S. military bases across the region and become a point of contention in the American midterm elections. Asked what he wanted to see happen in Iran, Johnson said he hoped Iranians would rise up against their government and that Iran would never acquire a nuclear weapon.
"I want to see the Ayatollahs on the dustbin of history," he said.

The Delhi Government on Thursday (November 19, 2026) launched the ‘Ehsaas 2026’ Mental Health and Well-Being Policy for schools and higher educational institutions in the national capital. The policy aims to ensure one counsellor for every 500 students, besides providing helplines and mental and emotional support services.
Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa were present at the launch.
The policy seeks to raise awareness about mental health and encourage students, teachers and parents to speak openly about the subject, making mental and emotional well-being an integral part of education.
Under the policy, special attention will be given to examination pressure, academic stress, anxiety, depression, interpersonal relationships and challenges related to digital behaviour. Students dealing with the pressure of board and entrance examinations will also receive guidance and support, according to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).
The policy also provides for opportunities for students to develop stress-management and social-emotional skills, while sensitising teachers and parents to recognise early signs of mental health concerns. It also emphasises confidential mechanisms for reporting bullying, identity-based discrimination and cyberbullying, timely action on complaints, and protection from harassment for those filing complaints, according to an official statement.
Equal support for all children
The Lieutenant-Governor said making mental health and emotional well-being an integral part of education was the need of the hour. At a time when young people were facing increasing stress, the Delhi government’s initiative was timely and commendable.
Mr. Sandhu said, “Every child’s feelings, aspirations and needs matter. No child should face discrimination on the basis of their background, abilities or circumstances. Children with disabilities and those from disadvantaged communities must be given equal opportunities, acceptance and support.”
He added that responsibility for mental health rested not only with students but also with teachers, parents and school management.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the policy had been introduced keeping in mind the mental health and overall well-being of students and would be implemented across schools and higher educational institutions in Delhi.
She said ‘Ehsaas’ would give millions of students studying in Delhi’s schools and colleges an opportunity to move forward with greater mental and emotional resilience. “The Delhi government wants every child to progress in life with happiness, positivity and confidence, and to know that the government, teachers and parents will stand by them through every challenge,” she said.
Six-tier mechanism
According to an official statement, the ‘Ehsaas’ policy will have a six-tier escalation mechanism to ensure student safety and address serious mental health crises. The mechanism will include the class teacher, school counsellor/first responder, school head/wellness team, District Well-Being Centre, hospital/emergency mental health services and relevant statutory agencies.
Students will have access to specialised mental health services through District Well-Being Centres established at the district level. These centres will provide psychological assessments, therapeutic interventions and psychiatric consultations.
“Schools will be responsible for early identification, initial psychosocial support and referrals, while clinical assessments and treatment will be handled by trained specialists, ensuring that students who need help receive appropriate care in time,” the statement further added.
Staff to receive training
Education Minister Ashish Sood said the government took up the issue after a school student attempted suicide a few days ago. Following the incident, he wrote to school principals and held discussions with them and mental health experts to work towards a comprehensive policy.
He said the policy was an important initiative to understand children’s emotional needs, listen to them and provide appropriate support. He also thanked the Art of Living, UNESCO, IHBAS and expert institutions for their contribution to developing the policy.
Mr. Sood said teachers, parents, principals, Educational and Vocational Guidance Counsellors (EVGCs), officials, drivers and other support staff would be trained to identify early changes in children’s behaviour and respond with sensitivity and appropriate support.
Four key pillars
The ‘Ehsaas’ policy is based on four key pillars. The first, the “Whole-Institution Approach”, seeks to make mental health part of an institution’s overall culture, with the participation of students, teachers, faculty, institutional heads, hostel staff and parents, according to the CMO.
The second pillar, Proactive and Preventive Care, focuses on identifying early signs of mental health concerns, promoting social-emotional and life skills, and building mental resilience.
The third, System-Level Accountability and Governance, seeks to ensure clearly defined responsibilities within institutions, staff training, capacity building and accountability of institutional leadership.
The fourth pillar, Ethical Safety and Rights-Based Support, will protect students’ dignity, privacy and confidentiality, ensure age-appropriate consent for minors and respect the autonomy of adult students.

Scientists use special tests to understand how autistic people see, hear, and process information. But many of these tests require participants to understand complex spoken rules, speak their answers out loud or fill out long written questionnaires. For instance, a standard perception study might ask a participant to watch a screen and say out loud which direction a cluster of dots is moving. A non-verbal autistic child cannot provide the required response, automatically excluding them from the research.
Now, Boston University researchers have tried to study perception without relying on language or conventional test-taking skills by turning a sensory test originally developed for rodents into a non-verbal online video game that adolescents across the autism spectrum can learn and play.
This holds special promise for India. A non-verbal, remote game bypasses the need to translate complex clinical instructions into dozens of regional languages, and allows researchers to reach autistic individuals far beyond the major metros where specialist centres are concentrated.

UK to explore even closer ties with EU after agreeing deal, says Burnham
- Published
Andy Burnham said the UK will discuss possible options for even closer ties with the EU, after agreeing a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.
The prime minister said it was a "good day" for Britain and Europe, adding the Treasury believes the deal could boost the UK economy by up to £17bn a year.
European Council President António Costa said the EU remains "open to have the closest possible relationship" with the UK.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal "isn't fair" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a "betrayal of the British people".
Legislation to implement the deal is expected to be introduced in the UK Parliament next week.
Burnham arrived in Brussels to finalise the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU, which originally began under former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.
The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.
The UK government believes the changes will cut costs for businesses and could bring prices down for shoppers, while critics argue the change will make the UK a "rule taker" from Brussels rather than a rule maker.
The new youth experience scheme will allow up to 100,000 18 to 31 year olds from the EU to travel, work and study in the UK for up to three years. The same number of young Britons will be allowed into Europe.
The two sides want to ensure that opportunities under the annual scheme will be available to young people by no later than January 2030.
A further six months is available to discuss a deal on tuition fees, which could prove to be a potential stumbling block.
There have been calls from the European side for fees to be reduced for EU students at British universities. The joint statement says any agreement would also be for UK students in the EU.
